files.title: Axiom audit
The density action `P`, and `P⋆ = P*`

decls.name: abs_rpow_add3_le
decls.statement: theorem abs_rpow_add3_le {w₁ w₂ w₃ u₁ u₂ u₃ p : ℝ} (h1 : 0 ≤ w₁) (h2 : 0 ≤ w₂) (h3 : 0 ≤ w₃) (hw : w₁ + w₂ + w₃ = 1) (hp : 1 ≤ p) : |w₁ * u₁ + w₂ * u₂ + w₃ * u₃| ^ p ≤ w₁ * |u₁| ^ p + w₂ * |u₂| ^ p + w₃ * |u₃| ^ p
decls.doc: Jensen's inequality for a three-atom probability and the convex `t ↦ |t|^p`, `p ≥ 1`.

decls.name: mact_vanish_offChain
decls.statement: theorem mact_vanish_offChain (hrow : RowOnChain S cap) {nu : St → ℝ} (hnu : ∀ x, ¬ OnChain cap x → nu x = 0) {y : St} (hy : ¬ OnChain cap y) : mact S cap nu y = 0
decls.doc: Off the chain the transported measure vanishes: no edge of the chain leaves it.

decls.name: dens
decls.statement: noncomputable def dens (u : St → ℝ) (y : St) : ℝ
decls.doc: **The density action** `Pu := d((uλ)T)/dλ`, in closed form: the transported measure `(uλ)T` of `Balance.mact`, divided by `λ`.

decls.name: w1
decls.statement: noncomputable def w1 (k : ℕ) : ℝ
decls.doc: The reversed one-step law: the decrement weight, read backwards.

decls.name: w2
decls.statement: noncomputable def w2 (k : ℕ) : ℝ
decls.doc: The reversed one-step law: the doubling weight, read backwards.

decls.name: w3
decls.statement: noncomputable def w3 (k : ℕ) : ℝ
decls.doc: The reversed one-step law: the target-row weight, read backwards.

decls.name: w1_nonneg
decls.statement: theorem w1_nonneg (k : ℕ) : 0 ≤ L.w1 k

decls.name: w2_nonneg
decls.statement: theorem w2_nonneg (k : ℕ) : 0 ≤ L.w2 k

decls.name: w3_nonneg
decls.statement: theorem w3_nonneg (k : ℕ) : 0 ≤ L.w3 k

decls.name: w_sum
decls.statement: theorem w_sum {k : ℕ} (hk : OnChain cap (.lad k)) : L.w1 k + L.w2 k + L.w3 k = 1
decls.doc: **The reversed law is a probability at every state of the chain.** This is the balance equation `λT = λ` divided by `λ_k`, and it is the only place invariance enters.

decls.name: dens_sink
decls.statement: theorem dens_sink (u : St → ℝ) : L.dens u .sink = u (.lad 0)
decls.doc: `P` at the sink: the wrap is the only incoming edge, so `(Pu)(s_f) = u(s₀)`.

decls.name: dens_lad
decls.statement: theorem dens_lad (u : St → ℝ) (k : ℕ) : L.dens u (.lad k) = L.w1 k * u (.lad (k + 1)) + L.w2 k * u (.lad (k / 2)) + L.w3 k * u .sink
decls.doc: `P` at a ladder state, as a three-atom average.

decls.name: lam_mul_dens
decls.statement: theorem lam_mul_dens (hrow : RowOnChain S cap) (u : St → ℝ) (y : St) : L.lam y * L.dens u y = mact S cap (fun x => L.lam x * u x) y
decls.doc: **`λ·Pu = (uλ)T`.** On the chain this is the definition with the division cleared; off it both sides vanish, `λ` by `Stat.vanish` and the transported measure by `mact_vanish_offChain`.

decls.name: dens_const
decls.statement: theorem dens_const (hrow : RowOnChain S cap) {y : St} (hy : OnChain cap y) : L.dens (fun _ => (1 : ℝ)) y = 1
decls.doc: **`P` fixes the constants** on the chain: the reversed law is a probability.

decls.name: summable_abs_lad_mul
decls.statement: theorem summable_abs_lad_mul {g : St → ℝ} (hg : ∀ x, 0 ≤ g x) (hs : Summable fun x => L.lam x * g x) : Summable fun k : ℕ => |L.lam (.lad k) * g (.lad k)|
decls.doc: `λ·g` is absolutely ladder-summable whenever `g` has finite `λ`-integral.

decls.name: tsum_lam_dens
decls.statement: theorem tsum_lam_dens (hrow : RowOnChain S cap) {g : St → ℝ} (hg : ∀ x, 0 ≤ g x) (hs : Summable fun x => L.lam x * g x) : ∑' y, L.lam y * L.dens g y = ∑' x, L.lam x * g x
decls.doc: **`∫ Pg dλ = ∫ g dλ`** at every non-negative `g` with finite `λ`-integral: the transported measure has the same total mass.

decls.name: summable_lam_dens
decls.statement: theorem summable_lam_dens (hrow : RowOnChain S cap) {g : St → ℝ} (hg : ∀ x, 0 ≤ g x) (hs : Summable fun x => L.lam x * g x) : Summable fun y => L.lam y * L.dens g y

decls.name: abs_rpow_dens_le
decls.statement: theorem abs_rpow_dens_le {p : ℝ} (hp : 1 ≤ p) (u : St → ℝ) {y : St} (hy : OnChain cap y) : |L.dens u y| ^ p ≤ L.dens (fun z => |u z| ^ p) y
decls.doc: **Jensen for `P`**, at every state of the chain: `|Pu|^p ≤ P(|u|^p)` for `p ≥ 1`.

decls.name: mass_dens_le
decls.statement: theorem mass_dens_le (hrow : RowOnChain S cap) {p : ℝ} (hp : 1 ≤ p) {u : St → ℝ} (hs : Summable fun x => |u x| ^ p * L.lam x) : L.mass p (L.dens u) ≤ L.mass p u
decls.doc: **`P` is a contraction of `L^p(λ)`**, `p ∈ [1,∞)` — the mirror of `Stat.mass_pstar_le`, and what makes `P` an operator of `L²(λ)`.

decls.name: tsum_dens_mul
decls.statement: theorem tsum_dens_mul (hrow : RowOnChain S cap) {u : St → ℝ} (hu : Summable fun k : ℕ => |L.lam (.lad k) * u (.lad k)|) {v : St → ℝ} (hv : ∃ C, ∀ x, |v x| ≤ C) : ∑' y, L.lam y * L.dens u y * v y = ∑' x, L.lam x * u x * pstar S cap v x
decls.doc: **`⟨Pu,v⟩_λ = ⟨u,P⋆v⟩_λ` at bounded `v`.** This is `lem:doubling_operator`(1)'s adjoint clause on the plain-real layer, and it is also the characterisation of `Pu` as a Radon–Nikodym derivative: taking `v = 1_{\{y\}}` reads off `λ(y)(Pu)(y) = ((uλ)T)(\{y\})`.

decls.name: abs_rpow_two'
decls.statement: theorem abs_rpow_two' (t : ℝ) : |t| ^ (2 : ℝ) = t ^ 2
decls.doc: `|t|^{(2:ℝ)} = t^2`: the bridge between the `rpow` form of `Stat.mass` and the natural power the summability estimates are written in.

decls.name: abs_pstar_le
decls.statement: theorem abs_pstar_le (f : St → ℝ) (x : St) : |pstar S cap f x| ≤ pstar S cap (fun y => |f y|) x
decls.doc: `|P⋆f| ≤ P⋆|f|`: Jensen at `p = 1`.

decls.name: summable_mass_pstar
decls.statement: theorem summable_mass_pstar {p : ℝ} (hp : 1 ≤ p) {f : St → ℝ} (hs : Summable fun x => |f x| ^ p * L.lam x) : Summable fun x => |pstar S cap f x| ^ p * L.lam x
decls.doc: `P⋆` preserves the `L^p` summability of the mass — the summability half of `Stat.mass_pstar_le`.

decls.name: summable_mass_dens
decls.statement: theorem summable_mass_dens (hrow : RowOnChain S cap) {p : ℝ} (hp : 1 ≤ p) {u : St → ℝ} (hs : Summable fun x => |u x| ^ p * L.lam x) : Summable fun x => |L.dens u x| ^ p * L.lam x
decls.doc: `P` preserves the `L^p` summability of the mass — the summability half of `Stat.mass_dens_le`.

decls.name: summable_lam_mul_mul
decls.statement: theorem summable_lam_mul_mul {a b : St → ℝ} (ha : Summable fun x => |a x| ^ (2 : ℝ) * L.lam x) (hb : Summable fun x => |b x| ^ (2 : ℝ) * L.lam x) : Summable fun x => L.lam x * |a x| * |b x|
decls.doc: The Cauchy–Schwarz-free product bound: `2|a||b| ≤ a² + b²`, summed against `λ`.

decls.name: summable_abs_lad_of_sq
decls.statement: theorem summable_abs_lad_of_sq {u : St → ℝ} (hu : Summable fun x => |u x| ^ (2 : ℝ) * L.lam x) : Summable fun k : ℕ => |L.lam (.lad k) * u (.lad k)|
decls.doc: `λ·u` is absolutely ladder-summable whenever `u ∈ L²(λ)`.

decls.name: tsum_dens_mul_sq
decls.statement: theorem tsum_dens_mul_sq (hrow : RowOnChain S cap) {u v : St → ℝ} (hu : Summable fun x => |u x| ^ (2 : ℝ) * L.lam x) (hv : Summable fun x => |v x| ^ (2 : ℝ) * L.lam x) : ∑' y, L.lam y * L.dens u y * v y = ∑' x, L.lam x * u x * pstar S cap v x
decls.doc: **`⟨Pu,v⟩_λ = ⟨u,P⋆v⟩_λ` at `u, v ∈ L²(λ)`** — `lem:doubling_operator`(1)'s adjoint clause, at the paper's own hypothesis.

decls.name: tsum_lam_pstar_sq
decls.statement: theorem tsum_lam_pstar_sq (hrow : RowOnChain S cap) {v : St → ℝ} (hv : Summable fun x => |v x| ^ (2 : ℝ) * L.lam x) : ∑' x, L.lam x * pstar S cap v x = ∑' x, L.lam x * v x
decls.doc: **Invariance against a square-integrable test function.** `Stat.inv` is stated against bounded `f`; `u ≡ 1` in the adjoint identity, where `P1 = 1`, removes that restriction at `L²(λ)`.

decls.name: memLp_dens
decls.statement: theorem memLp_dens (hrow : RowOnChain S cap) {p : ℝ≥0∞} (hp1 : 1 ≤ p) (hpt : p ≠ ∞) {u : St → ℝ} (hu : MemLp u p L.mu) : MemLp (L.dens u) p L.mu
decls.doc: `P` maps `L^p(μ)` into itself, at every finite `p ≥ 1`.

decls.name: eLpNorm_dens_le
decls.statement: theorem eLpNorm_dens_le (hrow : RowOnChain S cap) {p : ℝ≥0∞} (hp1 : 1 ≤ p) (hpt : p ≠ ∞) {u : St → ℝ} (hu : MemLp u p L.mu) : eLpNorm (L.dens u) p L.mu ≤ eLpNorm u p L.mu
decls.doc: **`P` is a contraction of `L^p(μ)`**, `p ∈ [1,∞)` — the `eLpNorm` form of `Stat.mass_dens_le`.

files.title: `P⋆ = P*` on `L²(λ)`, and `‖P⋆ⁿ − Π‖ = β̂ₙ`

decls.name: inner_eq_tsum
decls.statement: theorem inner_eq_tsum (F G : Lp ℝ 2 L.mu) : ⟪F, G⟫_ℝ = ∑' x, L.lam x * F x * G x
decls.doc: **The Bochner half of the `LpLayer` dictionary.** `⟪F,G⟫_{L²(μ)} = ∑' x, λ(x)F(x)G(x)`.

decls.name: inner_eq_tsum_of_ae
decls.statement: theorem inner_eq_tsum_of_ae {F G : Lp ℝ 2 L.mu} {f g : St → ℝ} (hF : ⇑F =ᵐ[L.mu] f) (hG : ⇑G =ᵐ[L.mu] g) : ⟪F, G⟫_ℝ = ∑' x, L.lam x * f x * g x
decls.doc: The same, read against any representatives: off the chain `λ` vanishes, so a.e.

decls.name: dens_add
decls.statement: theorem dens_add (u v : St → ℝ) : L.dens (u + v) = L.dens u + L.dens v

decls.name: dens_smul
decls.statement: theorem dens_smul (c : ℝ) (u : St → ℝ) : L.dens (c • u) = c • L.dens u

decls.name: dens_congr_onChain
decls.statement: theorem dens_congr_onChain {u v : St → ℝ} (h : ∀ x, OnChain cap x → u x = v x) (y : St) : L.dens u y = L.dens v y
decls.doc: **`P` descends to `λ`-classes**, and unlike `P⋆` it needs no hypothesis to do so: each of its three weights carries the factor `λ` of the state it reads (`Stat.w1`, `Stat.w2`, `Stat.w3`), so a state off the chain is read with weight zero.

decls.name: densLp
decls.statement: noncomputable def densLp (hrow : RowOnChain S cap) (F : Lp ℝ 2 L.mu) : Lp ℝ 2 L.mu
decls.doc: `P` acting on `L²(μ)`, as a map of the space into itself.

decls.name: coeFn_densLp
decls.statement: theorem coeFn_densLp (hrow : RowOnChain S cap) (F : Lp ℝ 2 L.mu) : ⇑(L.densLp hrow F) =ᵐ[L.mu] L.dens ⇑F

decls.name: norm_densLp_le
decls.statement: theorem norm_densLp_le (hrow : RowOnChain S cap) (F : Lp ℝ 2 L.mu) : ‖L.densLp hrow F‖ ≤ ‖F‖

decls.name: densLp_add
decls.statement: theorem densLp_add (hrow : RowOnChain S cap) (F G : Lp ℝ 2 L.mu) : L.densLp hrow (F + G) = L.densLp hrow F + L.densLp hrow G

decls.name: densLp_smul
decls.statement: theorem densLp_smul (hrow : RowOnChain S cap) (c : ℝ) (F : Lp ℝ 2 L.mu) : L.densLp hrow (c • F) = c • L.densLp hrow F

decls.name: densL2
decls.statement: noncomputable def densL2 (hrow : RowOnChain S cap) : Lp ℝ 2 L.mu →L[ℝ] Lp ℝ 2 L.mu
decls.doc: **`P` as a bounded linear operator on `L²(μ)`**, of norm at most `1` — the mirror of `Stat.pstarL2`, and the operator the paper's `β̂ₙ` is measured on.

decls.name: densL2_apply
decls.statement: @[simp] theorem densL2_apply (hrow : RowOnChain S cap) (F : Lp ℝ 2 L.mu) : L.densL2 hrow F = L.densLp hrow F

decls.name: coeFn_densL2
decls.statement: theorem coeFn_densL2 (hrow : RowOnChain S cap) (F : Lp ℝ 2 L.mu) : ⇑(L.densL2 hrow F) =ᵐ[L.mu] L.dens ⇑F

decls.name: norm_densL2_le
decls.statement: theorem norm_densL2_le (hrow : RowOnChain S cap) : ‖L.densL2 hrow‖ ≤ 1

decls.name: inner_densL2_left
decls.statement: theorem inner_densL2_left (hrow : RowOnChain S cap) (U V : Lp ℝ 2 L.mu) : ⟪L.densL2 hrow U, V⟫_ℝ = ⟪U, L.pstarL2 hrow V⟫_ℝ
decls.doc: **`⟪PU, V⟫ = ⟪U, P⋆V⟫` on `L²(μ)`** — `Stat.tsum_dens_mul_sq` read through the inner product.

decls.name: adjoint_pstarL2
decls.statement: theorem adjoint_pstarL2 (hrow : RowOnChain S cap) : ContinuousLinearMap.adjoint (L.pstarL2 hrow) = L.densL2 hrow
decls.doc: **The adjoint clause of `lem:doubling_operator`(1).** The density action is the `L²(λ)`-adjoint of the function action.

decls.name: adjoint_densL2
decls.statement: theorem adjoint_densL2 (hrow : RowOnChain S cap) : ContinuousLinearMap.adjoint (L.densL2 hrow) = L.pstarL2 hrow
decls.doc: The same identity read the other way: `P* = P⋆`.

decls.name: piL2
decls.statement: noncomputable def piL2 : Lp ℝ 2 L.mu →L[ℝ] Lp ℝ 2 L.mu
decls.doc: **`Π`, the `λ`-mean projection** of `L²(μ)`: `ΠF = (∫F dλ)·1`.

decls.name: piL2_apply
decls.statement: @[simp] theorem piL2_apply (F : Lp ℝ 2 L.mu) : L.piL2 F = ⟪L.oneLp, F⟫_ℝ • L.oneLp

decls.name: inner_oneLp_self
decls.statement: theorem inner_oneLp_self : ⟪L.oneLp, L.oneLp⟫_ℝ = 1
decls.doc: `⟪1,1⟫ = 1`: `λ` is a probability.

decls.name: piL2_mul_piL2
decls.statement: theorem piL2_mul_piL2 : L.piL2 * L.piL2 = L.piL2
decls.doc: **`Π` is idempotent.**

decls.name: adjoint_piL2
decls.statement: theorem adjoint_piL2 : ContinuousLinearMap.adjoint L.piL2 = L.piL2
decls.doc: **`Π` is self-adjoint**, `λ` being a probability.

decls.name: piL2_mul_pstarL2
decls.statement: theorem piL2_mul_pstarL2 (hrow : RowOnChain S cap) : L.piL2 * L.pstarL2 hrow = L.piL2
decls.doc: `Π P⋆ = Π`: the function action preserves the `λ`-mean.

decls.name: pstarL2_mul_piL2
decls.statement: theorem pstarL2_mul_piL2 (hrow : RowOnChain S cap) : L.pstarL2 hrow * L.piL2 = L.piL2
decls.doc: `P⋆ Π = Π`: the function action fixes the constants.

decls.name: piL2_mul_densL2
decls.statement: theorem piL2_mul_densL2 (hrow : RowOnChain S cap) : L.piL2 * L.densL2 hrow = L.piL2
decls.doc: `Π P = Π`, read off the adjoint of `P Π = Π`.

decls.name: densL2_mul_piL2
decls.statement: theorem densL2_mul_piL2 (hrow : RowOnChain S cap) : L.densL2 hrow * L.piL2 = L.piL2
decls.doc: `P Π = Π`, read off the adjoint of `Π P⋆ = Π`.

decls.name: betaHat
decls.statement: noncomputable def betaHat (hrow : RowOnChain S cap) (n : ℕ) : ℝ
decls.doc: **`β̂ₙ := ‖Pⁿ − Π‖_{L²(λ)}`** — the mixing coefficient of `def:doubling_setting`, defined on the density action as the paper defines it.

decls.name: adjoint_densL2_pow_sub_piL2
decls.statement: theorem adjoint_densL2_pow_sub_piL2 (hrow : RowOnChain S cap) (n : ℕ) : ContinuousLinearMap.adjoint ((L.densL2 hrow) ^ n - L.piL2) = (L.pstarL2 hrow) ^ n - L.piL2
decls.doc: `P⋆ⁿ − Π` is the adjoint of `Pⁿ − Π`.

decls.name: norm_pstarL2_pow_sub_piL2
decls.statement: theorem norm_pstarL2_pow_sub_piL2 (hrow : RowOnChain S cap) (n : ℕ) : ‖(L.pstarL2 hrow) ^ n - L.piL2‖ = L.betaHat hrow n
decls.doc: **`‖P⋆ⁿ − Π‖_{L²(λ)} = β̂ₙ` for every `n ≥ 0`** — the trailing clause of `lem:doubling_operator`(1).

files.title: The measure action, its duality with `P⋆`, and the pointwise balance equations

decls.name: dblW
decls.statement: noncomputable def dblW (S : Setting) (cap : Option ℕ) (j : ℕ) : ℝ
decls.doc: The doubling weight out of the ladder state `j ≥ 1`: `ε(j)` when the edge `j → 2j` survives the truncation, `0` when it has been deleted.

decls.name: decW
decls.statement: noncomputable def decW (S : Setting) (cap : Option ℕ) (j : ℕ) : ℝ
decls.doc: The decrement weight out of the ladder state `j ≥ 1`: `1 − ε(j)` when the doubling edge survives, `1` when it has been deleted and the decrement carries the whole mass.

decls.name: dblW_nonneg
decls.statement: theorem dblW_nonneg {j : ℕ} (hj : 1 ≤ j) : 0 ≤ dblW S cap j

decls.name: decW_nonneg
decls.statement: theorem decW_nonneg {j : ℕ} (hj : 1 ≤ j) : 0 ≤ decW S cap j

decls.name: dblW_add_decW
decls.statement: theorem dblW_add_decW {j : ℕ} : dblW S cap j + decW S cap j = 1
decls.doc: The one-step law out of a ladder state is a probability.

decls.name: dblW_le_one
decls.statement: theorem dblW_le_one {j : ℕ} (hj : 1 ≤ j) : dblW S cap j ≤ 1

decls.name: decW_le_one
decls.statement: theorem decW_le_one {j : ℕ} (hj : 1 ≤ j) : decW S cap j ≤ 1

decls.name: pstar_lad_succ_weights
decls.statement: theorem pstar_lad_succ_weights {f : St → ℝ} (j : ℕ) : pstar S cap f (.lad (j + 1)) = dblW S cap (j + 1) * f (.lad (2 * (j + 1))) + decW S cap (j + 1) * f (.lad j)
decls.doc: `P⋆` at a ladder state, with the two weights named: this is `pstar_lad_succ` with the `if` pushed into `dblW` and `decW`.

decls.name: row_zero
decls.statement: theorem row_zero (S : Setting) : S.row 0 = 0
decls.doc: The target row vanishes at `0`: `row_supp` forces `1 ≤ j` at every non-zero entry.

decls.name: mact
decls.statement: noncomputable def mact (S : Setting) (cap : Option ℕ) (nu : St → ℝ) : St → ℝ | .lad k => nu (.lad (k + 1)) * decW S cap (k + 1) + (if 1 ≤ k ∧ 2 ∣ k then nu (.lad (k / 2)) * dblW S cap (k / 2) else 0) + nu .sink * S.row k | .sink => nu (.lad 0) @[simp] theorem mact_sink (nu : St → ℝ) : mact S cap nu .sink = nu (.lad 0)
decls.doc: **The transported measure `νT`**, in closed form: one summand per kind of incoming edge.

decls.name: mact_lad
decls.statement: theorem mact_lad (nu : St → ℝ) (k : ℕ) : mact S cap nu (.lad k) = nu (.lad (k + 1)) * decW S cap (k + 1) + (if 1 ≤ k ∧ 2 ∣ k then nu (.lad (k / 2)) * dblW S cap (k / 2) else 0) + nu .sink * S.row k

decls.name: hasSum_mact
decls.statement: theorem hasSum_mact (S : Setting) (cap : Option ℕ) {nu : St → ℝ} (hsum : Summable fun k : ℕ => |nu (.lad k)|) {f : St → ℝ} (hf : ∃ C, ∀ x, |f x| ≤ C) : ∃ V : ℝ, HasSum (fun x => nu x * pstar S cap f x) V ∧ HasSum (fun y => mact S cap nu y * f y) V
decls.doc: **The duality identity, in `HasSum` form.** Both series converge, to the same value.

decls.name: tsum_mact
decls.statement: theorem tsum_mact (S : Setting) (cap : Option ℕ) {nu : St → ℝ} (hsum : Summable fun k : ℕ => |nu (.lad k)|) {f : St → ℝ} (hf : ∃ C, ∀ x, |f x| ≤ C) : ∑' x, nu x * pstar S cap f x = ∑' y, mact S cap nu y * f y
decls.doc: **The duality identity.** `∫ v d(νT) = ∫ P⋆v dν`.

decls.name: summable_mact
decls.statement: theorem summable_mact (S : Setting) (cap : Option ℕ) {nu : St → ℝ} (hsum : Summable fun k : ℕ => |nu (.lad k)|) {f : St → ℝ} (hf : ∃ C, ∀ x, |f x| ≤ C) : Summable fun y => mact S cap nu y * f y

decls.name: tsum_mact_eq
decls.statement: theorem tsum_mact_eq (S : Setting) (cap : Option ℕ) {nu : St → ℝ} (hsum : Summable fun k : ℕ => |nu (.lad k)|) : ∑' y, mact S cap nu y = ∑' x, nu x
decls.doc: The transported measure has the same total mass: `f = 1` in the duality, `P⋆1 = 1`.

decls.name: summable_abs_lad
decls.statement: theorem summable_abs_lad : Summable fun k : ℕ => |L.lam (.lad k)|
decls.doc: `λ` restricted to the ladder is absolutely summable — the hypothesis every use of the duality takes.

decls.name: mact_lam
decls.statement: theorem mact_lam (y : St) : mact S cap L.lam y = L.lam y
decls.doc: **`λT = λ`, pointwise.** The paper's invariance hypothesis is carried in `Stat` in the integral form against bounded test functions; testing it against the indicator of a single state and reading the duality identity on the other side gives the balance equation at that state.

decls.name: lam_sink
decls.statement: theorem lam_sink : L.lam .sink = L.lam (.lad 0)
decls.doc: The balance equation at the sink: `λ(s_f) = λ(s₀)`, the wrap being the only incoming edge.

decls.name: lam_lad
decls.statement: theorem lam_lad (k : ℕ) : L.lam (.lad k) = L.lam (.lad (k + 1)) * decW S cap (k + 1) + (if 1 ≤ k ∧ 2 ∣ k then L.lam (.lad (k / 2)) * dblW S cap (k / 2) else 0) + L.lam .sink * S.row k
decls.doc: The balance equation at a ladder state, written out.

files.title: The solutions of the cut balance form a `d`-dimensional space

decls.name: extend
decls.statement: noncomputable def extend (D : Decay) (d : ℕ) (b : ℕ → ℝ) (m : ℕ) : ℝ
decls.doc: The solution of `eq:doubling_avg` with boundary data `b` on `{0,…,d}`.

decls.name: extend_of_le
decls.statement: theorem extend_of_le (b : ℕ → ℝ) {m : ℕ} (h : m ≤ d) : D.extend d b m = b m

decls.name: extend_of_gt
decls.statement: theorem extend_of_gt (b : ℕ → ℝ) {m : ℕ} (h : d < m) : D.extend d b m = ∑ j ∈ window m, D.qm m j * D.extend d b j

decls.name: extend_cutBal
decls.statement: theorem extend_cutBal (b : ℕ → ℝ) (hd : 1 ≤ d) : D.CutBal d (D.extend d b) ⊤
decls.doc: `extend` solves the cut balance.

decls.name: extend_unique
decls.statement: theorem extend_unique {lam b : ℕ → ℝ} (h : D.CutBal d lam ⊤) (hd : 1 ≤ d) (hb : ∀ j ≤ d, lam j = b j) : ∀ m, lam m = D.extend d b m
decls.doc: Nothing else with the same boundary data solves it: the coordinate map is injective.

decls.name: extend_pos
decls.statement: theorem extend_pos (b : ℕ → ℝ) (hd : 1 ≤ d) (hb : ∀ j, 1 ≤ j → j ≤ d → 0 < b j) : ∀ m, 1 ≤ m → 0 < D.extend d b m
decls.doc: Positivity of the sequence is positivity of the boundary data.

decls.name: extend_add
decls.statement: theorem extend_add (b₁ b₂ : ℕ → ℝ) (m : ℕ) : D.extend d (fun j => b₁ j + b₂ j) m = D.extend d b₁ m + D.extend d b₂ m
decls.doc: The extension is additive in the boundary data.

decls.name: extend_smul
decls.statement: theorem extend_smul (t : ℝ) (b : ℕ → ℝ) (m : ℕ) : D.extend d (fun j => t * b j) m = t * D.extend d b m
decls.doc: The extension is homogeneous in the boundary data.

decls.name: extend_congr_high
decls.statement: theorem extend_congr_high (b₁ b₂ : ℕ → ℝ) (hb : ∀ j, d < 2 * j → j ≤ d → b₁ j = b₂ j) : ∀ m : ℕ, d < m → D.extend d b₁ m = D.extend d b₂ m
decls.doc: **The mechanism behind `ν_j = 0` for `2j ≤ d`.** Above the cut `d`, the solution does not see the boundary data at an index `j` with `2j ≤ d`: every window of an `m > d` starts at `⌈m/2⌉ ≥ (d+1)/2 > d/2`.

files.title: `lem:doubling_coupling`: two descents from one block reach the base block with nearly the same law

decls.name: block_eq
decls.statement: theorem block_eq (i ℓ : ℕ) : block i ℓ = Finset.Ico (2 ^ i * ℓ) (2 * (2 ^ i * ℓ))
decls.doc: `I_i(ℓ) = [a, 2a)` with `a = 2^i ℓ`.

decls.name: le_pow_mul
decls.statement: theorem le_pow_mul (i ℓ : ℕ) : ℓ ≤ 2 ^ i * ℓ

decls.name: coupling
decls.statement: theorem coupling {ℓ : ℕ} (hℓ : 20 ≤ ℓ) (hℓτ : 32 * D.c * D.tau ≤ (ℓ : ℝ)) : ∀ i : ℕ, ∀ y ∈ block i ℓ, ∀ y' ∈ block i ℓ, tvOn (Finset.Ico ℓ (2 * ℓ)) (D.exitLaw ℓ y) (D.exitLaw ℓ y') ≤ (1 - D.omeg) ^ i
decls.doc: **`eq:doubling_coupling`.** Two descents started in `I_i(ℓ)` reach the base block `[ℓ,2ℓ)` with laws at total variation at most `(1−ω)^i`.

decls.name: coupling_above
decls.statement: theorem coupling_above {ℓ : ℕ} (hℓ : 20 ≤ ℓ) (hℓτ : 32 * D.c * D.tau ≤ (ℓ : ℝ)) (i : ℕ) {m m' : ℕ} (hm : 2 ^ i * ℓ ≤ m) (hm' : 2 ^ i * ℓ ≤ m') : tvOn (Finset.Ico ℓ (2 * ℓ)) (D.exitLaw ℓ m) (D.exitLaw ℓ m') ≤ (1 - D.omeg) ^ i
decls.doc: **The coupling bound above a block.** Two descents started anywhere above `2^i ℓ` — not necessarily in the same block — reach the base block `[ℓ,2ℓ)` with laws at total variation at most `(1−ω)^i`.

files.title: The Cramér root

decls.name: psi
decls.statement: noncomputable def psi (c t : ℝ) : ℝ
decls.doc: `ψ(t) = c(2^t − 1) − t`, whose non-zero root is the Cramér exponent `p_*`.

decls.name: psi_zero
decls.statement: theorem psi_zero (c : ℝ) : psi c 0 = 0

decls.name: two_rpow_eq
decls.statement: theorem two_rpow_eq (t : ℝ) : (2 : ℝ) ^ t = exp (t * log 2)
decls.doc: `2^t = exp (t · ln 2)`.

decls.name: two_rpow_pos
decls.statement: theorem two_rpow_pos (t : ℝ) : (0 : ℝ) < (2 : ℝ) ^ t

decls.name: log_two_pos
decls.statement: theorem log_two_pos : (0 : ℝ) < log 2

decls.name: two_log_two_gt_one
decls.statement: theorem two_log_two_gt_one : (1 : ℝ) < 2 * log 2
decls.doc: `2 ln 2 > 1`, the one numeric fact behind `two_rpow_gt_add_one`.

decls.name: two_rpow_gt_add_one
decls.statement: theorem two_rpow_gt_add_one {t : ℝ} (ht : 1 < t) : t + 1 < (2 : ℝ) ^ t
decls.doc: **`eq:doubling_cramer_ineq`, the engine.** `2^t > t + 1` for every `t > 1`.

decls.name: hasDerivAt_two_rpow
decls.statement: theorem hasDerivAt_two_rpow (t : ℝ) : HasDerivAt (fun x : ℝ => (2 : ℝ) ^ x) ((2 : ℝ) ^ t * log 2) t

decls.name: hasDerivAt_psi
decls.statement: theorem hasDerivAt_psi (c t : ℝ) : HasDerivAt (psi c) (c * ((2 : ℝ) ^ t * log 2) - 1) t

decls.name: deriv_psi
decls.statement: theorem deriv_psi (c : ℝ) : deriv (psi c) = fun t => c * ((2 : ℝ) ^ t * log 2) - 1

decls.name: continuous_two_rpow
decls.statement: theorem continuous_two_rpow : Continuous fun t : ℝ => (2 : ℝ) ^ t

decls.name: continuous_psi
decls.statement: theorem continuous_psi (c : ℝ) : Continuous (psi c)

decls.name: psi_strictConvexOn
decls.statement: theorem psi_strictConvexOn {c : ℝ} (hc : 0 < c) : StrictConvexOn ℝ univ (psi c)
decls.doc: `ψ` is strictly convex on `ℝ`, for every `c > 0`.

decls.name: psi_neg_of_mem_openSegment
decls.statement: theorem psi_neg_of_mem_openSegment {c : ℝ} (hc : 0 < c) {a b t : ℝ} (ha : psi c a = 0) (hb : psi c b = 0) (hab : a ≠ b) (ht : t ∈ openSegment ℝ a b) : psi c t < 0

decls.name: psi_neg_of_between
decls.statement: theorem psi_neg_of_between {c : ℝ} (hc : 0 < c) {a b t : ℝ} (ha : psi c a = 0) (hb : psi c b = 0) (hab : a < b) (h1 : a < t) (h2 : t < b) : psi c t < 0

decls.name: psi_pos_of_outside
decls.statement: theorem psi_pos_of_outside {c : ℝ} (hc : 0 < c) {a b t : ℝ} (ha : psi c a = 0) (hb : psi c b = 0) (hab : a < b) (ht : t < a ∨ b < t) : 0 < psi c t
decls.doc: Outside the closed interval spanned by two roots, `ψ` is strictly positive.

decls.name: psi_no_three_roots
decls.statement: theorem psi_no_three_roots {c : ℝ} (hc : 0 < c) {a b e : ℝ} (hab : a < b) (hbe : b < e) (ha : psi c a = 0) (hb : psi c b = 0) (he : psi c e = 0) : False
decls.doc: `ψ` has no three distinct roots.

decls.name: cramer_root_unique
decls.statement: theorem cramer_root_unique {c : ℝ} (hc : 0 < c) {p q : ℝ} (hp0 : p ≠ 0) (hq0 : q ≠ 0) (hp : psi c p = 0) (hq : psi c q = 0) : p = q
decls.doc: **Uniqueness.** `ψ` has at most one root other than `0`.

decls.name: psi_pos_of_log_eq
decls.statement: theorem psi_pos_of_log_eq {c : ℝ} (hc : c * log 2 = 1) {t : ℝ} (ht : t ≠ 0) : 0 < psi c t
decls.doc: At `c = 1/ln 2` the only root is `0`: `ψ(t) > 0` for `t ≠ 0`.

decls.name: psi_pos_atTop
decls.statement: theorem psi_pos_atTop {c : ℝ} (hc : 0 < c) : ∃ T : ℝ, 0 < T ∧ ∀ t, T ≤ t → 0 < psi c t
decls.doc: `ψ(T) > 0` for `T` far enough to the right: the exponential beats the line.

decls.name: psi_pos_atBot
decls.statement: theorem psi_pos_atBot {c : ℝ} (hc : 0 < c) : ∃ T : ℝ, T < 0 ∧ ∀ t, t ≤ T → 0 < psi c t
decls.doc: `ψ(T) > 0` for `T` far enough to the left, where `c(2^T − 1) > −c`.

decls.name: cramer_root_exists
decls.statement: theorem cramer_root_exists {c : ℝ} (hc : 0 < c) (hne : c * log 2 ≠ 1) : ∃ p : ℝ, p ≠ 0 ∧ psi c p = 0 ∧ (0 < p ↔ c * log 2 < 1)
decls.doc: The root exists whenever `c ln 2 ≠ 1`, and its sign is that of `1 − c ln 2`.

decls.name: cramer_root_gt_one
decls.statement: theorem cramer_root_gt_one {c p : ℝ} (hc : 0 < c) (hc1 : c < 1) (hp0 : p ≠ 0) (hp : psi c p = 0) : 1 < p
decls.doc: **`lem:doubling_cramer_root`(1), second equivalence, `⟸`.** `c < 1` forces `p_* > 1`.

decls.name: cramer_lt_one_of_root_gt_one
decls.statement: theorem cramer_lt_one_of_root_gt_one {c p : ℝ} (hc : 0 < c) (hp : psi c p = 0) (hp1 : 1 < p) : c < 1
decls.doc: **`lem:doubling_cramer_root`(1), second equivalence, `⟹`.** `p_* > 1` forces `c < 1`.

decls.name: cramer_root_pos_iff
decls.statement: theorem cramer_root_pos_iff {c p : ℝ} (hc : 0 < c) (hne : c * log 2 ≠ 1) (hp0 : p ≠ 0) (hp : psi c p = 0) : 0 < p ↔ c * log 2 < 1
decls.doc: **`lem:doubling_cramer_root`(1), first equivalence.**

decls.name: cramer_form
decls.statement: theorem cramer_form {c p : ℝ} (hp0 : p ≠ 0) (hp : psi c p = 0) : c * (((2 : ℝ) ^ p - 1) / p) = 1
decls.doc: **`eq:doubling_cramer_form`.** `c(τ−1)/p_* = 1`.

decls.name: cramer_kernel_integral
decls.statement: theorem cramer_kernel_integral {c p : ℝ} (hp0 : p ≠ 0) (hp : psi c p = 0) : (∫ v in (0 : ℝ)..1, c * log 2 * (2 : ℝ) ^ (p * v)) = 1
decls.doc: **`lem:doubling_cramer_root`(2), the kernel.** `∫₀¹ c ln 2 · 2^{p v} dv = 1`.

decls.name: cramer_ineq
decls.statement: theorem cramer_ineq (hc : 0 < c) (hc1 : c < 1) (hp0 : p ≠ 0) (hp : psi c p = 0) : 2 < (2 : ℝ) ^ p ∧ p + 1 < (2 : ℝ) ^ p ∧ p + 2 < 2 * (2 : ℝ) ^ p ∧ p + 3 < 4 * (2 : ℝ) ^ p
decls.doc: **`eq:doubling_cramer_ineq`.** At `0 < c < 1`, with `τ := 2^{p_*}`: `τ > 2`, `τ > p_*+1`, `2τ > p_*+2` and `4τ > p_*+3`.

files.title: Cut balance

decls.name: lam_mul_dirac_eq
decls.statement: theorem lam_mul_dirac_eq (L : Stat S cap) (j : ℕ) : (fun x => L.lam x * dirac j x) = (fun x => if x = St.lad j then L.lam (St.lad j) else 0)
decls.doc: `λ` against a point mass is the mass of the point.

decls.name: hasSum_lam_mul_dirac
decls.statement: theorem hasSum_lam_mul_dirac (L : Stat S cap) (j : ℕ) : HasSum (fun x => L.lam x * dirac j x) (L.lam (.lad j))

decls.name: summable_lam_mul_dirac
decls.statement: theorem summable_lam_mul_dirac (L : Stat S cap) (j : ℕ) : Summable (fun x => L.lam x * dirac j x)

decls.name: tsum_lam_mul_dirac
decls.statement: theorem tsum_lam_mul_dirac (L : Stat S cap) (j : ℕ) : ∑' x, L.lam x * dirac j x = L.lam (.lad j)

decls.name: tsum_lam_mul_cutFn
decls.statement: theorem tsum_lam_mul_cutFn (L : Stat S cap) {m : ℕ} (hdm : S.d < m) (hD : HasDouble cap m) : ∑' x, L.lam x * cutFn S m x = 0
decls.doc: The `λ`-integral of the per-cut defect vanishes: this is invariance, tested against `1_A`.

decls.name: cut_balance
decls.statement: theorem cut_balance (L : Stat S cap) {m : ℕ} (hdm : S.d < m) (hD : HasDouble cap m) : L.lam (.lad m) * (1 - S.eps m) = ∑ j ∈ window m, L.lam (.lad j) * S.eps j
decls.doc: **`eq:doubling_cut`.** The mass leaving the cut at `m` by decrement equals the mass entering it from the window below by doubling.

decls.name: CutBalanceSeq
decls.statement: def CutBalanceSeq (S : Setting) (lam : ℕ → ℝ) (M₁ : ℕ∞) : Prop
decls.doc: The recursion `eq:doubling_cut` as a predicate on a bare real sequence, with no invariance and no normalisation.

decls.name: cutBalanceSeq_of_stat
decls.statement: theorem cutBalanceSeq_of_stat (L : Stat S none) : CutBalanceSeq S (fun j => L.lam (.lad j)) ⊤
decls.doc: An invariant probability of the loop closure gives a sequence satisfying the recursion everywhere: the bridge from `Stat` to `CutBalanceSeq`.

files.title: Notation for the decay estimates, and the averaging form of the cut balance

decls.statement: lemma, and it is what lets `cor:doubling_truncation` feed `λ^K` in later. ## Hypothesis checklist | paper hypothesis | here | | | `s = 1` | ✓ carried, as the shape of `Decay.eps` | | `0 < c < 1` | ✓ carried (`Decay.c_pos`, `Decay.c_lt_one`) | | `p = p_*` the Cramér root | ✓ carried (`Decay.root`, `Decay.p_ne`) | | `m > d` in the averaging | ✓ carried; `1 ≤ m` is what the proof needs and is implied | | `(λ_j)` positive | ⚠ weakened: the identities of `lem:doubling_averaging` are linear and need no sign | Provenance: mathlib `fabf563a` (tag `v4.31.0`), pinned via `lakefile.toml`. -/ namespace GFNBounds.Doubling open Real / Cramér equation `c(2^p − 1) = p`. -/ structure Decay

decls.name: p_gt_one
decls.statement: theorem p_gt_one : 1 < D.p
decls.doc: `p_* > 1` at `0 < c < 1` (`lem:doubling_cramer_root`(1)).

decls.name: p_pos
decls.statement: theorem p_pos : 0 < D.p

decls.name: tau
decls.statement: noncomputable def tau : ℝ

decls.name: tau_gt_two
decls.statement: theorem tau_gt_two : 2 < D.tau

decls.name: tau_pos
decls.statement: theorem tau_pos : 0 < D.tau

decls.name: cramer
decls.statement: theorem cramer : D.c * ((D.tau - 1) / D.p) = 1
decls.doc: **`eq:doubling_cramer_form`.** `c(τ−1)/p = 1`.

decls.name: eps
decls.statement: noncomputable def eps (j : ℕ) : ℝ
decls.doc: `ε(j) = c/(j+1)`, the family at `s = 1`.

decls.name: eps_eq
decls.statement: theorem eps_eq (j : ℕ) : D.eps j = D.c / ((j : ℝ) + 1)

decls.name: eps_pos
decls.statement: theorem eps_pos (j : ℕ) : 0 < D.eps j

decls.name: eps_le_half
decls.statement: theorem eps_le_half {j : ℕ} (hj : 1 ≤ j) : D.eps j ≤ D.c / 2

decls.name: one_sub_eps_pos
decls.statement: theorem one_sub_eps_pos {j : ℕ} (hj : 1 ≤ j) : 0 < 1 - D.eps j

decls.name: qm
decls.statement: noncomputable def qm (m j : ℕ) : ℝ
decls.doc: `q_m(j) = c/((j+1)(1−ε(m)))`, the cut weights of `eq:doubling_window`.

decls.name: qm_eq
decls.statement: theorem qm_eq (m j : ℕ) : D.qm m j = D.c / (((j : ℝ) + 1) * (1 - D.eps m))

decls.name: qm_pos
decls.statement: theorem qm_pos {m : ℕ} (hm : 1 ≤ m) (j : ℕ) : 0 < D.qm m j

decls.name: wm
decls.statement: noncomputable def wm (m j : ℕ) : ℝ
decls.doc: `w_m(j) = q_m(j)(m/j)^p`, the rescaled cut weights.

decls.name: wm_pos
decls.statement: theorem wm_pos {m j : ℕ} (hm : 1 ≤ m) (hj : 1 ≤ j) : 0 < D.wm m j

decls.name: wm_nonneg
decls.statement: theorem wm_nonneg {m j : ℕ} (hm : 1 ≤ m) (hj : 1 ≤ j) : 0 ≤ D.wm m j

decls.name: R0
decls.statement: noncomputable def R0 (m : ℕ) : ℝ
decls.doc: `R_0(m) = Σ_{j ∈ W(m)} w_m(j)`, the total weight of the window — `eq:doubling_R` at `α = 0`.

decls.name: uu
decls.statement: noncomputable def uu (lam : ℕ → ℝ) (m : ℕ) : ℝ
decls.doc: The rescaled profile `u_m := λ_m m^p` of `def:doubling_decay_notation`.

decls.name: Phi
decls.statement: noncomputable def Phi (α : ℝ) (j : ℕ) : ℝ

decls.name: Ralpha
decls.statement: noncomputable def Ralpha (α : ℝ) (m : ℕ) : ℝ
decls.doc: `R_α(m)` of `eq:doubling_R`.

decls.name: delta
decls.statement: def delta (m : ℕ) : ℕ
decls.doc: The parity `δ(m) = m − 2⌊m/2⌋`.

decls.name: delta_lt_two
decls.statement: theorem delta_lt_two (m : ℕ) : delta m < 2

decls.name: block
decls.statement: def block (i ℓ : ℕ) : Finset ℕ
decls.doc: The dyadic block `I_i(ℓ) = [2^i ℓ, 2^{i+1} ℓ)`.

decls.name: mem_block
decls.statement: theorem mem_block {i ℓ n : ℕ} : n ∈ block i ℓ ↔ 2 ^ i * ℓ ≤ n ∧ n < 2 ^ (i + 1) * ℓ

decls.name: CutBal
decls.statement: def CutBal (d : ℕ) (lam : ℕ → ℝ) (M₁ : ℕ∞) : Prop
decls.doc: `eq:doubling_cut` as a predicate on a bare sequence, with `ε` the family at `s = 1`.

decls.name: cutBal_of_setting
decls.statement: theorem cutBal_of_setting {S : Setting} {lam : ℕ → ℝ} {M₁ : ℕ∞} (heps : ∀ j, S.eps j = D.eps j) (h : CutBalanceSeq S lam M₁) : D.CutBal S.d lam M₁
decls.doc: The bridge: a `Setting` whose `ε` is the family at `s = 1` gives `Decay.CutBal`.

decls.name: one_le_of_mem_window'
decls.statement: theorem one_le_of_mem_window' {m j : ℕ} (hm : 1 ≤ m) (hj : j ∈ window m) : 1 ≤ j
decls.doc: Every index of `W(m)` is a positive integer, `m` being positive.

decls.name: avg_of_cutBal
decls.statement: theorem avg_of_cutBal {d : ℕ} {lam : ℕ → ℝ} {M₁ : ℕ∞} (h : D.CutBal d lam M₁) {m : ℕ} (hm : 1 ≤ m) (hdm : d < m) (hM : (m : ℕ∞) ≤ M₁) : lam m = ∑ j ∈ window m, D.qm m j * lam j
decls.doc: **`eq:doubling_avg`.** Dividing `eq:doubling_cut` by `1 − ε(m)` turns the balance across the cut into an *average* of the sequence over the window below it.

decls.name: uavg_of_avg
decls.statement: theorem uavg_of_avg {lam : ℕ → ℝ} {m : ℕ} (hm : 1 ≤ m) (h : lam m = ∑ j ∈ window m, D.qm m j * lam j) : D.uu lam m = ∑ j ∈ window m, D.wm m j * D.uu lam j
decls.doc: **`eq:doubling_uavg`, first line.** The same average, on the rescaled profile.

decls.name: sum_wm
decls.statement: theorem sum_wm (m : ℕ) : ∑ j ∈ window m, D.wm m j = D.R0 m
decls.doc: **`eq:doubling_uavg`, second line.** The total weight of the window is `R_0(m)`, by definition of `R_0` — recorded so that the descent recursion may cite it.

decls.name: uavg_of_cutBal
decls.statement: theorem uavg_of_cutBal {d : ℕ} {lam : ℕ → ℝ} {M₁ : ℕ∞} (h : D.CutBal d lam M₁) {m : ℕ} (hm : 1 ≤ m) (hdm : d < m) (hM : (m : ℕ∞) ≤ M₁) : D.uu lam m = ∑ j ∈ window m, D.wm m j * D.uu lam j
decls.doc: **`lem:doubling_averaging`, both items at once.**

files.title: The descent chain, as a recursion

decls.name: descW
decls.statement: noncomputable def descW (D : Decay) (ℓ : ℕ) (g : ℕ → ℝ) (m : ℕ) : ℝ
decls.doc: **The descent transform.** `descW D ℓ g m = E(Z_ℓ · g(Y_{N_ℓ}) | Y_0 = m)`, written as an unnormalized recursion: the `R_0` of the transition law and the `R_0` of the weight `Z_ℓ` cancel.

decls.name: descW_of_lt
decls.statement: theorem descW_of_lt {ℓ : ℕ} (g : ℕ → ℝ) {m : ℕ} (h : m < 2 * ℓ) : D.descW ℓ g m = g m

decls.name: descW_of_ge
decls.statement: theorem descW_of_ge {ℓ : ℕ} (g : ℕ → ℝ) {m : ℕ} (h : ¬ m < 2 * ℓ) : D.descW ℓ g m = ∑ j ∈ window m, D.wm m j * D.descW ℓ g j

decls.name: descOne
decls.statement: noncomputable def descOne (ℓ m : ℕ) : ℝ
decls.doc: `E(Z_ℓ | Y_0 = m)`, the expected weight of a descent.

decls.name: descOne_of_lt
decls.statement: theorem descOne_of_lt {ℓ m : ℕ} (h : m < 2 * ℓ) : D.descOne ℓ m = 1

decls.name: descOne_of_ge
decls.statement: theorem descOne_of_ge {ℓ m : ℕ} (h : ¬ m < 2 * ℓ) : D.descOne ℓ m = ∑ j ∈ window m, D.wm m j * D.descOne ℓ j

decls.name: le_of_mem_window_of_ge
decls.statement: theorem le_of_mem_window_of_ge {ℓ m j : ℕ} (hm : 2 * ℓ ≤ m) (hj : j ∈ window m) : ℓ ≤ j
decls.doc: Every index of the window of an `m ≥ 2ℓ` is at least `ℓ`: this is `⌈m/2⌉ ≥ ℓ`, and it is where `lem:doubling_descent`(2) — the descent lands in `[ℓ,2ℓ)` — enters.

decls.name: descW_uu
decls.statement: theorem descW_uu {ℓ d : ℕ} {lam : ℕ → ℝ} {M₁ : ℕ∞} (h : D.CutBal d lam M₁) (hℓ : d < 2 * ℓ) : ∀ m : ℕ, (m : ℕ∞) ≤ M₁ → D.uu lam m = D.descW ℓ (D.uu lam) m
decls.doc: **`eq:doubling_pathid`.** The rescaled profile is the fixed point of the descent transform: `u_m = E(Z_ℓ u_{Y_{N_ℓ}} | Y_0 = m)`.

decls.name: descW_between
decls.statement: theorem descW_between {ℓ : ℕ} (hℓ1 : 1 ≤ ℓ) {g : ℕ → ℝ} {a b : ℝ} (hab : ∀ j, ℓ ≤ j → j < 2 * ℓ → a ≤ g j ∧ g j ≤ b) : ∀ m : ℕ, ℓ ≤ m → a * D.descOne ℓ m ≤ D.descW ℓ g m ∧ D.descW ℓ g m ≤ b * D.descOne ℓ m
decls.doc: **The sandwich.** A function bounded between `a` and `b` on the base block `[ℓ,2ℓ)` has its descent transform bounded between `a·E(Z_ℓ)` and `b·E(Z_ℓ)`.

decls.name: decay_block
decls.statement: theorem decay_block {ℓ d : ℕ} {lam : ℕ → ℝ} {M₁ : ℕ∞} (h : D.CutBal d lam M₁) (hℓ : d < 2 * ℓ) (hℓ1 : 1 ≤ ℓ) {Z₁ Z₂ : ℝ} (hlo : ∀ y : ℕ, ℓ ≤ y → Z₁ ≤ D.descOne ℓ y) (hhi : ∀ y : ℕ, ℓ ≤ y → D.descOne ℓ y ≤ Z₂) {a b : ℝ} (ha : 0 ≤ a) (hab : ∀ j, ℓ ≤ j → j < 2 * ℓ → a ≤ D.uu lam j ∧ D.uu lam j ≤ b) {m : ℕ} (hm : ℓ ≤ m) (hM : (m : ℕ∞) ≤ M₁) : a * Z₁ ≤ D.uu lam m ∧ D.uu lam m ≤ b * Z₂
decls.doc: **`eq:doubling_block`.** One block of the profile bounds every index above it, within the two-sided bound on `E(Z_ℓ)` that `lem:doubling_product` supplies.

decls.name: uu_bounded
decls.statement: theorem uu_bounded {ℓ d : ℕ} {lam : ℕ → ℝ} (h : D.CutBal d lam ⊤) (hpos : ∀ j, 1 ≤ j → 0 < lam j) (hℓ : d < 2 * ℓ) (hℓ1 : 1 ≤ ℓ) {Z₁ Z₂ : ℝ} (hZ1 : 0 < Z₁) (hZ1' : Z₁ ≤ 1) (hZ2 : 1 ≤ Z₂) (hlo : ∀ y : ℕ, ℓ ≤ y → Z₁ ≤ D.descOne ℓ y) (hhi : ∀ y : ℕ, ℓ ≤ y → D.descOne ℓ y ≤ Z₂) : ∃ c₁ c₂ : ℝ, 0 < c₁ ∧ c₁ ≤ c₂ ∧ ∀ j : ℕ, 1 ≤ j → c₁ ≤ D.uu lam j ∧ D.uu lam j ≤ c₂
decls.doc: **`eq:doubling_decay`, in the `u` variable.** The rescaled profile is bounded above and below by positive constants, on the whole ladder.

decls.name: decay_two_sided
decls.statement: theorem decay_two_sided {ℓ d : ℕ} {lam : ℕ → ℝ} (h : D.CutBal d lam ⊤) (hpos : ∀ j, 1 ≤ j → 0 < lam j) (hℓ : d < 2 * ℓ) (hℓ1 : 1 ≤ ℓ) {Z₁ Z₂ : ℝ} (hZ1 : 0 < Z₁) (hZ1' : Z₁ ≤ 1) (hZ2 : 1 ≤ Z₂) (hlo : ∀ y : ℕ, ℓ ≤ y → Z₁ ≤ D.descOne ℓ y) (hhi : ∀ y : ℕ, ℓ ≤ y → D.descOne ℓ y ≤ Z₂) : ∃ c₁ c₂ : ℝ, 0 < c₁ ∧ c₁ ≤ c₂ ∧ ∀ j : ℕ, 1 ≤ j → c₁ * (j : ℝ) ^ (-D.p) ≤ lam j ∧ lam j ≤ c₂ * (j : ℝ) ^ (-D.p)
decls.doc: **`eq:doubling_decay`.** `c₁ j^{−p_*} ≤ λ_j ≤ c₂ j^{−p_*}` for every `j ≥ 1`.

files.title: The exit law of a descent, as a recursion, and its strong Markov property

decls.name: kern
decls.statement: noncomputable def kern (y j : ℕ) : ℝ
decls.doc: The one-step transition law of the descent chain, `k_y(j) = w_y(j)/R₀(y)`.

decls.name: window_nonempty
decls.statement: theorem window_nonempty {m : ℕ} (hm : 2 ≤ m) : (window m).Nonempty
decls.doc: The window is non-empty from `m = 2` on: `⌈m/2⌉ < m`.

decls.name: R0_pos
decls.statement: theorem R0_pos {m : ℕ} (hm : 2 ≤ m) : 0 < D.R0 m
decls.doc: `R₀(m) > 0` at `m ≥ 2`: it is a sum of positive terms over a non-empty window.

decls.name: kern_nonneg
decls.statement: theorem kern_nonneg {m : ℕ} (hm : 2 ≤ m) {j : ℕ} (hj : j ∈ window m) : 0 ≤ D.kern m j

decls.name: sum_kern
decls.statement: theorem sum_kern {m : ℕ} (hm : 2 ≤ m) : ∑ j ∈ window m, D.kern m j = 1
decls.doc: The one-step law is a probability on the window.

decls.name: kern_ge
decls.statement: theorem kern_ge {z : ℕ} (hz : 2 ≤ z) (hR : D.R0 z ≤ 2) {j : ℕ} (hj : j ∈ window z) : D.c / (2 * ((j : ℝ) + 1)) ≤ D.kern z j
decls.doc: **Second bullet of the proof of `lem:doubling_doeblin`.** One step from a state `z` with `R₀(z) ≤ 2` gives every `j ∈ W(z)` mass at least `c/(2(j+1))`.

decls.name: descP
decls.statement: noncomputable def descP (D : Decay) (ℓ : ℕ) (g : ℕ → ℝ) (m : ℕ) : ℝ
decls.doc: **`E(g(Y_{N_ℓ}) | Y_0 = m)`**, as a recursion.

decls.name: descP_of_lt
decls.statement: theorem descP_of_lt {ℓ : ℕ} (g : ℕ → ℝ) {m : ℕ} (h : m < 2 * ℓ) : D.descP ℓ g m = g m

decls.name: descP_of_ge
decls.statement: theorem descP_of_ge {ℓ : ℕ} (g : ℕ → ℝ) {m : ℕ} (h : ¬ m < 2 * ℓ) : D.descP ℓ g m = ∑ j ∈ window m, D.kern m j * D.descP ℓ g j

decls.name: exitLaw
decls.statement: noncomputable def exitLaw (ℓ y j : ℕ) : ℝ
decls.doc: **The exit law** `π_y = P(Y_{N_ℓ} ∈ · | Y_0 = y)`.

decls.name: exitLaw_of_lt
decls.statement: theorem exitLaw_of_lt {ℓ y j : ℕ} (h : y < 2 * ℓ) : D.exitLaw ℓ y j = if y = j then 1 else 0

decls.name: exitLaw_of_ge
decls.statement: theorem exitLaw_of_ge {ℓ y : ℕ} (h : ¬ y < 2 * ℓ) (j : ℕ) : D.exitLaw ℓ y j = ∑ z ∈ window y, D.kern y z * D.exitLaw ℓ z j

decls.name: descP_eq_sum
decls.statement: theorem descP_eq_sum {ℓ : ℕ} (g : ℕ → ℝ) : ∀ y : ℕ, ℓ ≤ y → D.descP ℓ g y = ∑ z ∈ Finset.Ico ℓ (2 * ℓ), D.exitLaw ℓ y z * g z
decls.doc: **`lem:doubling_descent`(2), normalised.** The exit law is a law on the base block: `descP ℓ g y = ∑_{z ∈ [ℓ,2ℓ)} exitLaw ℓ y z · g z` for every `y ≥ ℓ`.

decls.name: exitLaw_nonneg
decls.statement: theorem exitLaw_nonneg {ℓ : ℕ} (hℓ : 1 ≤ ℓ) (j : ℕ) : ∀ y : ℕ, ℓ ≤ y → 0 ≤ D.exitLaw ℓ y j
decls.doc: The exit law is non-negative on the base block.

decls.name: descP_one
decls.statement: theorem descP_one {ℓ : ℕ} (hℓ : 1 ≤ ℓ) : ∀ y : ℕ, ℓ ≤ y → D.descP ℓ (fun _ => 1) y = 1
decls.doc: `descP ℓ 1 = 1`: the recursion preserves the constants, `k_y` being a probability.

decls.name: exitLaw_sum
decls.statement: theorem exitLaw_sum {ℓ y : ℕ} (hℓ : 1 ≤ ℓ) (hy : ℓ ≤ y) : ∑ z ∈ Finset.Ico ℓ (2 * ℓ), D.exitLaw ℓ y z = 1
decls.doc: **The exit law is a probability on `[ℓ,2ℓ)`.**

decls.name: descP_comp
decls.statement: theorem descP_comp {ℓ a : ℕ} (hla : ℓ ≤ a) (g : ℕ → ℝ) : ∀ y : ℕ, D.descP ℓ g y = D.descP a (fun z => D.descP ℓ g z) y
decls.doc: **The strong Markov property at the block-exit time**, in the recursion's own terms: descending to the base block `[ℓ,2ℓ)` is descending to the block `[a,2a)` and then continuing.

decls.name: exitLaw_mix
decls.statement: theorem exitLaw_mix {ℓ a : ℕ} (hla : ℓ ≤ a) {y : ℕ} (hy : a ≤ y) (k : ℕ) : D.exitLaw ℓ y k = ∑ z ∈ Finset.Ico a (2 * a), D.exitLaw a y z * D.exitLaw ℓ z k
decls.doc: **`π_y = ∑_{z ∈ [a,2a)} μ_y(z) π_z`.** The mixture identity of `lem:doubling_coupling`, third bullet, with `μ_y` the exit law from the block `[a,2a)` and `π` the exit laws to `[ℓ,2ℓ)`.

files.title: `lem:doubling_doeblin`: the exit from a block charges a fixed fraction of one reference law

decls.name: omeg
decls.statement: noncomputable def omeg : ℝ
decls.doc: **`ω := (c²/16) ln(5/4) ln(8/5)`**, the minorization constant of `lem:doubling_doeblin`.

decls.name: omeg_pos
decls.statement: theorem omeg_pos : 0 < D.omeg

decls.name: omeg_ge
decls.statement: theorem omeg_ge : 3 * D.c ^ 2 / 640 ≤ D.omeg
decls.doc: **An effective lower bound**: `ω ≥ 3c²/640`, from `ln(5/4) ≥ 1/5` and `ln(8/5) ≥ 3/8`.

decls.name: omeg_lt_one
decls.statement: theorem omeg_lt_one : D.omeg < 1

decls.name: omeg_le_case_one
decls.statement: theorem omeg_le_case_one : D.omeg ≤ D.c / 4 * Real.log (8 / 5)
decls.doc: `(c/4) ln(5/4) ≤ 1`, so `ω ≤ (c/4) ln(8/5)`: the two cases of the proof combine.

decls.name: varpi
decls.statement: noncomputable def varpi (a j : ℕ) : ℝ
decls.doc: `ϖ_i`, the probability on the integers of `[⌈5a/4⌉,2a)` proportional to `j ↦ 1/(j+1)`.

decls.name: varpi_nonneg
decls.statement: theorem varpi_nonneg {a : ℕ} (ha : 20 ≤ a) (j : ℕ) : 0 ≤ varpi a j

decls.name: varpi_of_not_mem
decls.statement: theorem varpi_of_not_mem {a j : ℕ} (h : j ∉ Jlow a) : varpi a j = 0

decls.name: varpi_sum
decls.statement: theorem varpi_sum {a : ℕ} (ha : 20 ≤ a) : ∑ z ∈ Finset.Ico a (2 * a), varpi a z = 1
decls.doc: `ϖ_i` is a probability on `I_{i−1}(ℓ) = [a,2a)`.

decls.name: varpi_le
decls.statement: theorem varpi_le {a : ℕ} (ha : 20 ≤ a) (j : ℕ) : D.c / 4 * Real.log (8 / 5) * varpi a j ≤ D.c / (2 * ((j : ℝ) + 1))
decls.doc: `ϖ_i(j) ≤ 2/(ln(8/5)(j+1))` on `J`: the normalising sum is at least `½ ln(8/5)`.

decls.name: R0_le_two_of
decls.statement: theorem R0_le_two_of (haτ : 32 * D.c * D.tau ≤ (a : ℝ)) (ha : 20 ≤ a) {z : ℕ} (hz : a ≤ z) : D.R0 z ≤ 2
decls.doc: `R₀(z) ≤ 2` at every state of the two blocks in play.

decls.name: doeblin_low
decls.statement: theorem doeblin_low (ha : 20 ≤ a) (haτ : 32 * D.c * D.tau ≤ (a : ℝ)) {y : ℕ} (h1 : 2 * a ≤ y) (h2 : y < (5 * a + 1) / 2) (j : ℕ) : D.c / 4 * Real.log (8 / 5) * varpi a j ≤ D.exitLaw a y j
decls.doc: **Third bullet of `lem:doubling_doeblin`.** A state `y ∈ I_i(ℓ)` below `⌈5a/2⌉` leaves the block, in one step, with law at least `(c/4)ln(8/5) ϖ_i`.

decls.name: doeblin
decls.statement: theorem doeblin (ha : 20 ≤ a) (haτ : 32 * D.c * D.tau ≤ (a : ℝ)) {y : ℕ} (h1 : 2 * a ≤ y) (h2 : y < 4 * a) (j : ℕ) : D.omeg * varpi a j ≤ D.exitLaw a y j
decls.doc: **`eq:doubling_doeblin`.** Every state of `I_i(ℓ) = [2a,4a)` leaves the block with law at least `ω ϖ_i`.

files.title: The drift of the backward chain, and when it is constant

decls.name: height
decls.statement: def height : St → ℝ | .lad j => (j : ℝ) | .sink => 0 @[simp] theorem height_lad (j : ℕ) : height (.lad j) = (j : ℝ)
decls.doc: The ladder height, the paper's `V` (`lem:doubling_ramp`): the index of a ladder state, and `0` at the sink.

decls.name: height_sink
decls.statement: @[simp] theorem height_sink : height .sink = 0

decls.name: height_pstar_sub
decls.statement: theorem height_pstar_sub {m : ℕ} (hm : 1 ≤ m) (h : HasDouble cap m) : pstar S cap height (.lad m) - height (.lad m) = S.eps m * ((m : ℝ) + 1) - 1
decls.doc: **`eq:doubling_drift`, for a free `ε`.** The one-step drift of the backward chain at a ladder state carrying its doubling edge is `ε(m)(m+1) − 1`.

decls.name: base_mul_epsCS
decls.statement: theorem base_mul_epsCS (c s : ℝ) (m : ℕ) : ((m : ℝ) + 1) * epsCS c s m = c * ((m : ℝ) + 1) ^ (1 - s)
decls.doc: `(m+1)·ε_{c,s}(m) = c(m+1)^{1−s}`, the drift coefficient of `eq:doubling_drift` isolated.

decls.name: drift_family
decls.statement: theorem drift_family (c s : ℝ) (m : ℕ) : epsCS c s m * ((m : ℝ) + 1) - 1 = c * ((m : ℝ) + 1) ^ (1 - s) - 1
decls.doc: **`eq:doubling_drift`.** On the family, the drift is `c(m+1)^{1−s} − 1`.

decls.name: drift_family_at_one
decls.statement: theorem drift_family_at_one {c : ℝ} (m : ℕ) : epsCS c 1 m * ((m : ℝ) + 1) - 1 = c - 1
decls.doc: The drift is **constant in `j`** at `s = 1`, where it equals `c − 1`.

decls.name: four_rpow
decls.statement: private theorem four_rpow (t : ℝ) : (4 : ℝ) ^ t = (2 : ℝ) ^ (2 * t)
decls.doc: Two evaluations of the base identity, used to run `prop:doubling_drift`'s "iff" backwards.

decls.name: drift_const_iff
decls.statement: theorem drift_const_iff {c s : ℝ} (hc : 0 < c) (hconst : ∀ i j : ℕ, 1 ≤ i → 1 ≤ j → c * ((i : ℝ) + 1) ^ (1 - s) - 1 = c * ((j : ℝ) + 1) ^ (1 - s) - 1) : s = 1
decls.doc: **The converse half of `prop:doubling_drift`.** If the drift does not depend on the ladder state, then `s = 1`.

decls.name: drift_const_of_eq_one
decls.statement: theorem drift_const_of_eq_one {c : ℝ} (i j : ℕ) : c * ((i : ℝ) + 1) ^ (1 - (1:ℝ)) - 1 = c * ((j : ℝ) + 1) ^ (1 - (1:ℝ)) - 1
decls.doc: The forward half: at `s = 1` the drift is the constant `c − 1`.

files.title: `lem:doubling_escape`, Step 1: the descent halves at a uniform rate

decls.name: sum_shift_ge
decls.statement: theorem sum_shift_ge {r : ℝ} (hr : 0 < r) {a b : ℕ} (hab : a ≤ b) : (((a : ℝ) + 1) ^ (-r) - ((b : ℝ) + 1) ^ (-r)) / r ≤ ∑ j ∈ Finset.Ico a b, ((j : ℝ) + 1) ^ (-r - 1)
decls.doc: **Shifted window comparison.** `((a+1)^{−r} − (b+1)^{−r})/r ≤ Σ_{j ∈ [a,b)} (j+1)^{−r−1}`.

decls.name: sqrt_two_lt
decls.statement: theorem sqrt_two_lt : Real.sqrt 2 < 1.415

decls.name: one_lt_sqrt_two
decls.statement: theorem one_lt_sqrt_two : (1 : ℝ) < Real.sqrt 2

decls.name: sqrt_two_pos
decls.statement: theorem sqrt_two_pos : (0 : ℝ) < Real.sqrt 2

decls.name: sqTau
decls.statement: noncomputable def sqTau : ℝ

decls.name: sqTau_sq
decls.statement: theorem sqTau_sq : D.sqTau ^ 2 = D.tau

decls.name: one_lt_sqTau
decls.statement: theorem one_lt_sqTau : 1 < D.sqTau

decls.name: sqTau_pos
decls.statement: theorem sqTau_pos : 0 < D.sqTau

decls.name: sqrt_two_rpow
decls.statement: theorem sqrt_two_rpow : (Real.sqrt 2) ^ D.p = D.sqTau

decls.name: gam
decls.statement: noncomputable def gam : ℝ
decls.doc: **`γ := √τ/(2(√τ+1))`** of `lem:doubling_escape`.

decls.name: gam_pos
decls.statement: theorem gam_pos : 0 < D.gam

decls.name: gam_lt_half
decls.statement: theorem gam_lt_half : D.gam < 1 / 2
decls.doc: `γ < ½`, as the statement of `lem:doubling_escape` asserts.

decls.name: quarter_lt_gam
decls.statement: theorem quarter_lt_gam : 1 / 4 < D.gam
decls.doc: `γ > ¼`, which is what makes the threshold `32cτ` cover `4cτ/y ≤ γ/2`.

decls.name: cramer_mul
decls.statement: theorem cramer_mul : D.c * (D.tau - 1) = D.p
decls.doc: `c(τ−1) = p_*`, the Cramér equation cleared of its denominator.

decls.name: one_lt_ctau
decls.statement: theorem one_lt_ctau : 1 < D.c * D.tau
decls.doc: `cτ > 1`: indeed `cτ = p_* + c` and `p_* > 1`.

decls.name: ctau_pos
decls.statement: theorem ctau_pos : 0 < D.c * D.tau

decls.name: two_gam_eq
decls.statement: theorem two_gam_eq : D.c * ((D.tau - D.sqTau) / D.p) = 2 * D.gam
decls.doc: **`2γ = c(τ−√τ)/p_*`**, the identity that turns the paper's window bound into `2γ`.

decls.name: half_rpow'
decls.statement: theorem half_rpow' {x : ℝ} (hx : 0 < x) : (x / 2) ^ (-D.p) = D.tau * x ^ (-D.p)

decls.name: foot_shift_ge
decls.statement: theorem foot_shift_ge {y : ℕ} (hy : 1 ≤ y) : D.tau * (y : ℝ) ^ (-D.p) * (1 - 4 * D.p / (y : ℝ)) ≤ ((((y + 1) / 2 : ℕ) : ℝ) + 1) ^ (-D.p)
decls.doc: **The foot of the halving window.** With `a = ⌈y/2⌉`, `(a+1)^{−p} ≥ τ y^{−p}(1 − 4p/y)`.

decls.name: head_shift_le
decls.statement: theorem head_shift_le {y : ℕ} (hy : 1 ≤ y) {z : ℝ} (hz : (y : ℝ) / Real.sqrt 2 ≤ z) : z ^ (-D.p) ≤ D.sqTau * (y : ℝ) ^ (-D.p)
decls.doc: **The head of the halving window.** Any `z ≥ y/√2` has `z^{−p} ≤ √τ y^{−p}`.

decls.name: wm_ge_shift
decls.statement: theorem wm_ge_shift {y j : ℕ} (hy : 1 ≤ y) (hj : 1 ≤ j) : D.c * (y : ℝ) ^ D.p * (((j : ℝ) + 1) ^ (-D.p - 1)) ≤ D.wm y j
decls.doc: `w_y(j) ≥ c y^{p}(j+1)^{−p−1}`, the paper's first inequality of Step 1.

decls.name: halveIco
decls.statement: noncomputable def halveIco (y : ℕ) : Finset ℕ
decls.doc: The halving window `{j : ⌈y/2⌉ ≤ j ≤ ⌊y/√2⌋}`, as an interval of integers.

decls.name: thirty_two_lt
decls.statement: theorem thirty_two_lt (hy : 32 * D.c * D.tau ≤ (y : ℝ)) : (32 : ℝ) < (y : ℝ)
decls.doc: The threshold used throughout: `32cτ ≤ y` forces `y > 32`, since `cτ > 1`.

decls.name: one_le_of_thr
decls.statement: theorem one_le_of_thr (hy : 32 * D.c * D.tau ≤ (y : ℝ)) : 1 ≤ y

decls.name: floor_lt_self
decls.statement: theorem floor_lt_self (hy : 32 * D.c * D.tau ≤ (y : ℝ)) : ⌊(y : ℝ) / Real.sqrt 2⌋₊ < y

decls.name: foot_le_floor
decls.statement: theorem foot_le_floor (hy : 32 * D.c * D.tau ≤ (y : ℝ)) : (y + 1) / 2 ≤ ⌊(y : ℝ) / Real.sqrt 2⌋₊
decls.doc: `⌈y/2⌉ ≤ ⌊y/√2⌋`: the halving window is non-empty.

decls.name: escape_sum
decls.statement: theorem escape_sum (hy : 32 * D.c * D.tau ≤ (y : ℝ)) : 2 * D.gam - 4 * D.c * D.tau / (y : ℝ) ≤ ∑ j ∈ halveIco y, D.wm y j
decls.doc: **`lem:doubling_escape`, Step 1, un-normalised.** The paper's display `Σ_{j=⌈y/2⌉}^{⌊y/√2⌋} w_y(j) ≥ 2γ − 4cτ/y`.

decls.name: escape
decls.statement: theorem escape (hy : 32 * D.c * D.tau ≤ (y : ℝ)) : D.gam ≤ (∑ j ∈ halveIco y, D.wm y j) / D.R0 y
decls.doc: **`eq:doubling_escape`.** `P(Y₁ ≤ y/√2 | Y₀ = y) ≥ γ`, the transition law of `lem:doubling_descent` being `w_y(j)/R₀(y)` on `W(y)`.

decls.name: halveIco_eq_filter
decls.statement: theorem halveIco_eq_filter (hy : 32 * D.c * D.tau ≤ (y : ℝ)) : halveIco y = (window y).filter (fun j : ℕ => (j : ℝ) * Real.sqrt 2 ≤ (y : ℝ))
decls.doc: The interval `halveIco y` is exactly `{j ∈ W(y) : j√2 ≤ y}`, so `escape` really does bound the transition probability of `eq:doubling_escape`.

decls.name: escape_filter
decls.statement: theorem escape_filter (hy : 32 * D.c * D.tau ≤ (y : ℝ)) : D.gam ≤ (∑ j ∈ (window y).filter (fun j : ℕ => (j : ℝ) * Real.sqrt 2 ≤ (y : ℝ)), D.wm y j) / D.R0 y
decls.doc: **`eq:doubling_escape`, in the paper's own words.**

decls.name: ell2
decls.statement: noncomputable def ell2 (D : Decay) (d : ℕ) : ℕ
decls.doc: **`ℓ₂`, made effective.** `ℓ₂ := max(d+1, ⌈16cτ⌉)`, so that `y ≥ 2ℓ ≥ 2ℓ₂` gives `y ≥ 32cτ`, which is all three of the paper's requirements at once.

decls.name: lt_ell2
decls.statement: theorem lt_ell2 (d : ℕ) : d < D.ell2 d

decls.name: thr_of_level
decls.statement: theorem thr_of_level {d ℓ y : ℕ} (hℓ : D.ell2 d ≤ ℓ) (hy : 2 * ℓ ≤ y) : 32 * D.c * D.tau ≤ (y : ℝ)

decls.name: escape_of_level
decls.statement: theorem escape_of_level {d ℓ y : ℕ} (hℓ : D.ell2 d ≤ ℓ) (hy : 2 * ℓ ≤ y) : D.gam ≤ (∑ j ∈ (window y).filter (fun j : ℕ => (j : ℝ) * Real.sqrt 2 ≤ (y : ℝ)), D.wm y j) / D.R0 y
decls.doc: **`eq:doubling_escape` at the level `ℓ`**, exactly as `lem:doubling_escape` states it: for every `ℓ ≥ ℓ₂` and every `y ≥ 2ℓ`, `P(Y₁ ≤ y/√2 | Y₀ = y) ≥ γ`.

files.title: The excursion maximum is bounded by the hitting time

decls.name: LadderStep
decls.statement: def LadderStep (cap : Option ℕ) (a b : ℕ) : Prop
decls.doc: One admissible step of the backward chain along the ladder: double, when that edge survives the cap, or decrement.

decls.name: LadderStep.le_succ_add_one
decls.statement: theorem LadderStep.le_succ_add_one {cap : Option ℕ} {a b : ℕ} (h : LadderStep cap a b) : a ≤ b + 1
decls.doc: **The first half of `lem:doubling_excursion`.** `X_{n+1} ≥ X_n − 1`, in the form `X_n ≤ X_{n+1} + 1`.

decls.name: excursion_le
decls.statement: theorem excursion_le {cap : Option ℕ} {x : ℕ → ℕ} (hstep : ∀ n, LadderStep cap (x n) (x (n + 1))) {σ : ℕ} (hσ : x σ = 0) : ∀ n, n ≤ σ → x n ≤ σ
decls.doc: **`eq:doubling_excursion`.** Along any admissible path reaching `0` at time `σ`, every value up to `σ` is at most `σ`: the excursion maximum is bounded by the hitting time.

files.title: The coefficients of the expansion of `R_α`

decls.name: A0
decls.statement: noncomputable def A0 : ℝ
decls.doc: `A₀` of `eq:doubling_AB`.

decls.name: A1
decls.statement: noncomputable def A1 : ℝ
decls.doc: `A₁ := A₀ − cτ` of `eq:doubling_AB`.

decls.name: Gam
decls.statement: noncomputable def Gam : ℝ
decls.doc: `Γ` of `eq:doubling_AB`.

decls.name: tau_sub_one_pos
decls.statement: theorem tau_sub_one_pos : 0 < D.tau - 1

decls.name: p_add_one_pos
decls.statement: theorem p_add_one_pos : 0 < D.p + 1

decls.name: c_mul_tau
decls.statement: theorem c_mul_tau : D.c * D.tau = D.p * D.tau / (D.tau - 1)
decls.doc: `c τ = p τ/(τ−1)`, from `c(τ−1) = p`.

decls.name: A_one_eq
decls.statement: theorem A_one_eq : D.A1 = D.p * (D.p + 3 - 4 * D.tau) / (2 * (D.p + 1) * (D.tau - 1))
decls.doc: **The closed form of `A₁`.** `A₁ = p(p+3−4τ)/(2(p+1)(τ−1))`.

decls.name: A_gap
decls.statement: theorem A_gap : D.A0 - D.A1 = D.c * D.tau
decls.doc: **`rem:doubling_parity`.** The two parities differ at order `1/m` by `A₀ − A₁ = cτ`.

decls.name: Gamma_pos
decls.statement: theorem Gamma_pos : 0 < D.Gam
decls.doc: **`eq:doubling_signs`, `Γ > 0`.**

decls.name: Gamma_lt_one
decls.statement: theorem Gamma_lt_one : D.Gam < 1
decls.doc: **`eq:doubling_signs`, `Γ < 1`.** The gap is `2τ − p − 2 > 0`, the third inequality of `eq:doubling_cramer_ineq`.

decls.name: A_zero_pos
decls.statement: theorem A_zero_pos : 0 < D.A0
decls.doc: **`eq:doubling_signs`, `A₀ > 0`.**

decls.name: A_one_neg
decls.statement: theorem A_one_neg : D.A1 < 0
decls.doc: **`eq:doubling_signs`, `A₁ < 0`.** The sign is `p + 3 − 4τ < 0`, the fourth inequality of `eq:doubling_cramer_ineq`.

files.title: The decay exponent is a Cramér root

decls.name: sum_Ico_rpow_sub_integral_le
decls.statement: theorem sum_Ico_rpow_sub_integral_le {q : ℝ} {a b : ℕ} (ha : 1 ≤ a) (hab : a ≤ b) : |(∑ j ∈ Finset.Ico a b, (j : ℝ) ^ q) - ∫ x in (a : ℝ)..(b : ℝ), x ^ q| ≤ |(a : ℝ) ^ q - (b : ℝ) ^ q|
decls.doc: `Σ_{j=a}^{b−1} j^q` against `∫_a^b x^q dx`, within `|a^q − b^q|`, for every real `q`.

decls.name: integral_rpow_window
decls.statement: theorem integral_rpow_window {p : ℝ} (hp : p ≠ 0) {a b : ℕ} (ha : 1 ≤ a) (hab : a ≤ b) : ∫ x in (a : ℝ)..(b : ℝ), x ^ (-p - 1) = ((a : ℝ) ^ (-p) - (b : ℝ) ^ (-p)) / p
decls.doc: The integral itself, at `q = −p−1`, `p ≠ 0`.

decls.name: tendsto_foot_atTop
decls.statement: theorem tendsto_foot_atTop : Tendsto (fun m : ℕ => (((m + 1) / 2 : ℕ) : ℝ)) atTop atTop
decls.doc: The foot of the window, `⌈m/2⌉`, is at least `m/2`, hence tends to `+∞`.

decls.name: tendsto_foot_ratio
decls.statement: theorem tendsto_foot_ratio : Tendsto (fun m : ℕ => (((m + 1) / 2 : ℕ) : ℝ) / (m : ℝ)) atTop (𝓝 (1 / 2))

decls.name: tendsto_mpow_foot
decls.statement: theorem tendsto_mpow_foot (p : ℝ) : Tendsto (fun m : ℕ => (m : ℝ) ^ p * (((m + 1) / 2 : ℕ) : ℝ) ^ (-p)) atTop (𝓝 ((2 : ℝ) ^ p))

decls.name: tendsto_windowPower
decls.statement: theorem tendsto_windowPower (hp : p ≠ 0) : Tendsto (fun m : ℕ => (m : ℝ) ^ p * ∑ j ∈ window m, (j : ℝ) ^ (-p - 1)) atTop (𝓝 (((2 : ℝ) ^ p - 1) / p))
decls.doc: **The rescaled window sum of the pure power.** `m^p Σ_{j∈W(m)} j^{−p−1} → (2^p − 1)/p`.

decls.name: windowWeight_pos
decls.statement: theorem windowWeight_pos {m j : ℕ} (hm : 1 ≤ m) (hj : j ∈ window m) : 0 < (m : ℝ) ^ p * (j : ℝ) ^ (-p) / ((j : ℝ) + 1)
decls.doc: The window weights `w_m(j) = m^p j^{−p}/(j+1)` are positive on the window.

decls.name: tendsto_windowV
decls.statement: theorem tendsto_windowV (hp : p ≠ 0) : Tendsto (fun m : ℕ => ∑ j ∈ window m, (m : ℝ) ^ p * (j : ℝ) ^ (-p) / ((j : ℝ) + 1)) atTop (𝓝 (((2 : ℝ) ^ p - 1) / p))
decls.doc: **`V(m) → (2^p−1)/p`.** The rescaled window sum with the true weights `1/(j+1)` in place of `1/j`: the two differ by a relative `1/(⌈m/2⌉+1)`.

decls.name: exponent_is_cramer_root
decls.statement: theorem exponent_is_cramer_root {c : ℝ} (hc : 0 < c) {d : ℕ} {lam : ℕ → ℝ} (hcut : ∀ m : ℕ, d < m → lam m * (1 - c / ((m : ℝ) + 1)) = ∑ j ∈ window m, lam j * (c / ((j : ℝ) + 1))) {A p : ℝ} (hA : 0 < A) (hp : p ≠ 0) (hlim : Tendsto (fun j : ℕ => lam j * (j : ℝ) ^ p) atTop (𝓝 A)) : psi c p = 0
decls.doc: **`prop:doubling_exponent`.** If a sequence satisfying `eq:doubling_cut` at every `m > d` has `λ_j j^p → A > 0`, then `p` is a root of the Cramér equation.

files.title: An explicit divergent family: the `√m` rate

decls.name: tailSeq_eq_tailMass
decls.statement: theorem tailSeq_eq_tailMass (m : ℕ) : tailSeq (fun j => L.lam (.lad j)) m = L.tailMass m
decls.doc: The bridge: on the loop closure the tail of `λ` as a sequence is `Stat.tailMass`.

decls.name: rayleigh_family
decls.statement: theorem rayleigh_family (D : Decay) {c₁ c₂ : ℝ} (hc1 : 0 < c₁) (hbelow : ∀ j : ℕ, 1 ≤ j → c₁ * (j : ℝ) ^ (-D.p) ≤ L.lam (.lad j)) (habove : ∀ j : ℕ, 1 ≤ j → L.lam (.lad j) ≤ c₂ * (j : ℝ) ^ (-D.p)) {m : ℕ} (hdm : S.d < m) (hhalf : (1 : ℝ) / 2 ≤ 1 - L.tailMass m) : c₁ * (m : ℝ) * L.mass 2 (fun x => L.centredTail m x - pstar S none (L.centredTail m) x) ≤ 4 * c₂ * (D.p - 1) * L.mass 2 (L.centredTail m)
decls.doc: **`eq:doubling_explicit`, squared and cleared of denominators.** `c₁ m ‖(Id−P⋆)f_m‖²_{L²(λ)} ≤ 4c₂(p−1) ‖f_m‖²_{L²(λ)}`, i.e.

decls.name: exists_rayleigh_family
decls.statement: theorem exists_rayleigh_family (D : Decay) {c₁ c₂ : ℝ} (hc1 : 0 < c₁) (hbelow : ∀ j : ℕ, 1 ≤ j → c₁ * (j : ℝ) ^ (-D.p) ≤ L.lam (.lad j)) (habove : ∀ j : ℕ, 1 ≤ j → L.lam (.lad j) ≤ c₂ * (j : ℝ) ^ (-D.p)) : ∃ m₂ : ℕ, S.d < m₂ ∧ ∀ m : ℕ, m₂ ≤ m → c₁ * (m : ℝ) * L.mass 2 (fun x => L.centredTail m x - pstar S none (L.centredTail m) x) ≤ 4 * c₂ * (D.p - 1) * L.mass 2 (L.centredTail m)
decls.doc: **`cor:doubling_family`.** The cut `m₂` past which the rate holds exists, because `L(m) → 0`.

files.title: The fixed points of the function action are the constants

decls.name: sq_pstar_le
decls.statement: theorem sq_pstar_le (f : St → ℝ) (x : St) : (pstar S cap f x) ^ 2 ≤ pstar S cap (fun y => (f y) ^ 2) x
decls.doc: **Jensen at one state.** `(P⋆f)(x)² ≤ P⋆(f²)(x)`: the one-step law is a probability and `t ↦ t²` is convex.

decls.name: pstar_sq_gap
decls.statement: theorem pstar_sq_gap (f : St → ℝ) {m : ℕ} (hm : 1 ≤ m) (hD : HasDouble cap m) : pstar S cap (fun y => (f y) ^ 2) (.lad m) - (pstar S cap f (.lad m)) ^ 2 = S.eps m * (1 - S.eps m) * (f (.lad (2 * m)) - f (.lad (m - 1))) ^ 2
decls.doc: **Equality in Jensen at a doubling state.** The gap is `ε(m)(1−ε(m))(f(2m) − f(m−1))²`.

decls.name: tsum_jensen_gap
decls.statement: theorem tsum_jensen_gap {f : St → ℝ} (hb : ∃ C, ∀ x, |f x| ≤ C) (hfix : pstar S cap f = f) : ∑' x, L.lam x * (pstar S cap (fun y => (f y) ^ 2) x - (pstar S cap f x) ^ 2) = 0
decls.doc: The `λ`-integral of the Jensen gap of a bounded fixed point vanishes.

decls.name: jensen_gap_zero
decls.statement: theorem jensen_gap_zero (L : Stat S cap) {f : St → ℝ} (hb : ∃ C, ∀ x, |f x| ≤ C) (hfix : pstar S cap f = f) {x : St} (hx : OnChain cap x) : pstar S cap (fun y => (f y) ^ 2) x - (pstar S cap f x) ^ 2 = 0
decls.doc: **Equality in Jensen, at every state of the chain.**

decls.name: fixed_const
decls.statement: theorem fixed_const (L : Stat S cap) {f : St → ℝ} (hb : ∃ C, ∀ x, |f x| ≤ C) (hfix : pstar S cap f = f) : ∀ x : St, OnChain cap x → f x = f (.lad 0)
decls.doc: **`eq:doubling_fixed`, the `P⋆` half.** A bounded fixed point of the function action is constant on the chain.

files.title: The fixed points of the density action are the constants

decls.name: eq_zero_of_three_nonneg
decls.statement: theorem eq_zero_of_three_nonneg {a b c : ℝ} (ha : 0 ≤ a) (hb : 0 ≤ b) (hc : 0 ≤ c) (h : a + b + c = 0) : a = 0
decls.doc: The first of three non-negative reals summing to zero is zero.

decls.name: eq_mean_of_var_zero
decls.statement: theorem eq_mean_of_var_zero {w₁ w₂ w₃ u₁ u₂ u₃ : ℝ} (h2 : 0 ≤ w₂) (h3 : 0 ≤ w₃) (hw : w₁ + w₂ + w₃ = 1) (hpos : 0 < w₁) (hgap : w₁ * u₁ ^ 2 + w₂ * u₂ ^ 2 + w₃ * u₃ ^ 2 = (w₁ * u₁ + w₂ * u₂ + w₃ * u₃) ^ 2) : u₁ = w₁ * u₁ + w₂ * u₂ + w₃ * u₃
decls.doc: **Equality in Jensen for a three-atom probability, at the first atom.** If the second moment of `(u₁,u₂,u₃)` against `(w₁,w₂,w₃)` equals the square of its mean, then every atom of positive weight carries the mean; this is that statement at the first atom.

decls.name: onChain_lad_of_le
decls.statement: theorem onChain_lad_of_le {j k : ℕ} (hjk : j ≤ k) (hk : OnChain cap (.lad k)) : OnChain cap (.lad j)
decls.doc: A ladder state below an on-chain ladder state is on the chain.

decls.name: w1_pos
decls.statement: theorem w1_pos {k : ℕ} (hk : OnChain cap (.lad k)) (hk1 : OnChain cap (.lad (k + 1))) : 0 < L.w1 k
decls.doc: The climbing weight of the reversed law is positive wherever the state above is on the chain: `w₁(j) = λ_{j+1}dec(j+1)/λ_j`, and `dec` never vanishes.

decls.name: dens_gap_zero
decls.statement: theorem dens_gap_zero (hrow : RowOnChain S cap) {u : St → ℝ} (hu : Summable fun x => |u x| ^ (2 : ℝ) * L.lam x) (hfix : ∀ x, OnChain cap x → L.dens u x = u x) {y : St} (hy : OnChain cap y) : L.dens (fun z => (u z) ^ 2) y = (L.dens u y) ^ 2
decls.doc: **The Jensen gap of `P` vanishes on the chain at a fixed point in `L²(λ)`.** The gap is non-negative pointwise and its `λ`-integral is zero, `P` preserving the `λ`-integral and `Pu = u` on the chain; a convergent sum of non-negative terms vanishing forces each term to.

decls.name: dens_fixed_const
decls.statement: theorem dens_fixed_const (hrow : RowOnChain S cap) {u : St → ℝ} (hu : Summable fun x => |u x| ^ (2 : ℝ) * L.lam x) (hfix : ∀ x, OnChain cap x → L.dens u x = u x) : ∀ x : St, OnChain cap x → u x = u (.lad 0)
decls.doc: **`eq:doubling_fixed`, the `P` half.** A fixed point of the density action in `L²(λ)` is constant on the chain.

decls.name: dens_fixed_of_const
decls.statement: theorem dens_fixed_of_const {u : St → ℝ} (hc : ∀ x, OnChain cap x → u x = u (.lad 0)) {y : St} (hy : OnChain cap y) : L.dens u y = u y
decls.doc: The converse inclusion: `P` fixes every function constant on the chain.

decls.name: pstar_fixed_of_const
decls.statement: theorem pstar_fixed_of_const (hrow : RowOnChain S cap) {u : St → ℝ} (hc : ∀ x, OnChain cap x → u x = u (.lad 0)) {y : St} (hy : OnChain cap y) : pstar S cap u y = u y
decls.doc: The converse inclusion for the function action: `P⋆` fixes every function constant on the chain.

decls.name: ker_eq_const
decls.statement: theorem ker_eq_const (hrow : RowOnChain S cap) {u : St → ℝ} (hu : Summable fun x => |u x| ^ (2 : ℝ) * L.lam x) : ((∀ x, OnChain cap x → L.dens u x = u x) ↔ (∀ x, OnChain cap x → u x = u (.lad 0))) ∧ ((∀ x, OnChain cap x → pstar S cap u x = u x) ↔ (∀ x, OnChain cap x → u x = u (.lad 0)))
decls.doc: **`eq:doubling_fixed`, both halves.** In `L²(λ)`, the fixed points of the density action and of the function action are exactly the functions constant on the chain — that is, `ℝ·1`.

files.title: `eq:doubling_windowsums`: two harmonic window sums, with explicit constants

decls.name: log_step_le
decls.statement: theorem log_step_le (j : ℕ) : Real.log ((j : ℝ) + 2) - Real.log ((j : ℝ) + 1) ≤ 1 / ((j : ℝ) + 1)
decls.doc: `log(j+2) − log(j+1) ≤ 1/(j+1)`: this is `log t ≤ t − 1` at `t = (j+2)/(j+1)`.

decls.name: harmonic_window_ge
decls.statement: theorem harmonic_window_ge {A B : ℕ} (hAB : A ≤ B) : Real.log ((B : ℝ) + 1) - Real.log ((A : ℝ) + 1) ≤ ∑ j ∈ Finset.Ico A B, 1 / ((j : ℝ) + 1)
decls.doc: **The comparison.** `log(B+1) − log(A+1) ≤ ∑_{j=A}^{B−1} 1/(j+1)`.

decls.name: Jlow
decls.statement: def Jlow (a : ℕ) : Finset ℕ
decls.doc: `J = {⌈5a/4⌉, …, 2a−1}`, the range carrying the reference law `ϖ_i`.

decls.name: Jhigh
decls.statement: def Jhigh (a : ℕ) : Finset ℕ
decls.doc: `J' = {2a, …, ⌈5a/2⌉−1}`, the range the second case of `lem:doubling_doeblin` steps into.

decls.name: mem_Jlow
decls.statement: theorem mem_Jlow {a j : ℕ} : j ∈ Jlow a ↔ (5 * a + 3) / 4 ≤ j ∧ j < 2 * a

decls.name: mem_Jhigh
decls.statement: theorem mem_Jhigh {a j : ℕ} : j ∈ Jhigh a ↔ 2 * a ≤ j ∧ j < (5 * a + 1) / 2

decls.name: Jlow_subset
decls.statement: theorem Jlow_subset (a : ℕ) : Jlow a ⊆ Finset.Ico a (2 * a)

decls.name: Jhigh_subset
decls.statement: theorem Jhigh_subset (a : ℕ) : Jhigh a ⊆ Finset.Ico (2 * a) (4 * a)

decls.name: Jlow_nonempty
decls.statement: theorem Jlow_nonempty {a : ℕ} (ha : 2 ≤ a) : (Jlow a).Nonempty

decls.name: Jhigh_nonempty
decls.statement: theorem Jhigh_nonempty {a : ℕ} (ha : 1 ≤ a) : (Jhigh a).Nonempty

decls.name: Jlow_subset_window
decls.statement: theorem Jlow_subset_window {a y : ℕ} (h1 : 2 * a ≤ y) (h2 : y < (5 * a + 1) / 2) : Jlow a ⊆ window y
decls.doc: **Third bullet of `lem:doubling_doeblin`.** A state of `I_i(ℓ)` below `⌈5a/2⌉` sees all of `J` in its window.

decls.name: Jhigh_subset_window
decls.statement: theorem Jhigh_subset_window {a y : ℕ} (h1 : (5 * a + 1) / 2 ≤ y) (h2 : y < 4 * a) : Jhigh a ⊆ window y
decls.doc: **Fourth bullet of `lem:doubling_doeblin`.** A state of `I_i(ℓ)` at or above `⌈5a/2⌉` sees all of `J'` in its window.

decls.name: log_five_four_ge
decls.statement: theorem log_five_four_ge : (1 : ℝ) / 5 ≤ Real.log (5 / 4)

decls.name: log_eight_five_ge
decls.statement: theorem log_eight_five_ge : (3 : ℝ) / 8 ≤ Real.log (8 / 5)

decls.name: log_five_four_lt_one
decls.statement: theorem log_five_four_lt_one : Real.log (5 / 4) < 1

decls.name: log_eight_five_lt_one
decls.statement: theorem log_eight_five_lt_one : Real.log (8 / 5) < 1

decls.name: log_five_four_pos
decls.statement: theorem log_five_four_pos : 0 < Real.log (5 / 4)

decls.name: log_eight_five_pos
decls.statement: theorem log_eight_five_pos : 0 < Real.log (8 / 5)

decls.name: sum_Jlow_ge
decls.statement: theorem sum_Jlow_ge {a : ℕ} (ha : 1 ≤ a) : Real.log (8 / 5) - 2 / (a : ℝ) ≤ ∑ j ∈ Jlow a, 1 / ((j : ℝ) + 1)
decls.doc: **First line of `eq:doubling_windowsums`.** `∑_{j ∈ J} 1/(j+1) ≥ ln(8/5) − 2/a`.

decls.name: sum_Jhigh_ge
decls.statement: theorem sum_Jhigh_ge {a : ℕ} (ha : 1 ≤ a) : Real.log (5 / 4) - 2 / (a : ℝ) ≤ ∑ j ∈ Jhigh a, 1 / ((j : ℝ) + 1)
decls.doc: **Second line of `eq:doubling_windowsums`.** `∑_{j ∈ J'} 1/(j+1) ≥ ln(5/4) − 2/a`.

decls.name: sum_Jlow_half
decls.statement: theorem sum_Jlow_half {a : ℕ} (ha : 20 ≤ a) : (1 / 2) * Real.log (8 / 5) ≤ ∑ j ∈ Jlow a, 1 / ((j : ℝ) + 1)
decls.doc: **The half-bounds.** At `a ≥ 20` the two sums are at least `½ln(8/5)` and `½ln(5/4)`.

decls.name: sum_Jhigh_half
decls.statement: theorem sum_Jhigh_half {a : ℕ} (ha : 20 ≤ a) : (1 / 2) * Real.log (5 / 4) ≤ ∑ j ∈ Jhigh a, 1 / ((j : ℝ) + 1)

decls.name: sum_Jlow_pos
decls.statement: theorem sum_Jlow_pos {a : ℕ} (ha : 20 ≤ a) : 0 < ∑ j ∈ Jlow a, 1 / ((j : ℝ) + 1)

files.title: Irreducibility, and why an invariant probability is positive

decls.name: Edge
decls.statement: inductive Edge (S : Setting) (cap : Option ℕ) : St → St → Prop
decls.doc: The positive transitions of `eq:doubling_policy`: the wrap `s₀ → s_f`, the decrement `j+1 → j`, the doubling `j+1 → 2(j+1)` where that edge survives the cap, and the target row `s_f → k` at every `k` the row charges.

decls.name: Reach
decls.statement: abbrev Reach (S : Setting) (cap : Option ℕ) : St → St → Prop
decls.doc: Reachability: the reflexive-transitive closure of `Edge`.

decls.name: ptFn
decls.statement: def ptFn (y : St) : St → ℝ
decls.doc: The point mass at an arbitrary state, generalizing `dirac`.

decls.name: ptFn_nonneg
decls.statement: theorem ptFn_nonneg (y x : St) : 0 ≤ ptFn y x

decls.name: ptFn_bounded
decls.statement: theorem ptFn_bounded (y : St) : ∃ C, ∀ x, |ptFn y x| ≤ C

decls.name: ptFn_self
decls.statement: @[simp] theorem ptFn_self (y : St) : ptFn y y = 1

decls.name: ptFn_of_ne
decls.statement: theorem ptFn_of_ne {y x : St} (h : x ≠ y) : ptFn y x = 0

decls.name: edge_pstar_pos
decls.statement: theorem edge_pstar_pos {x y : St} (h : Edge S cap x y) : 0 < pstar S cap (ptFn y) x
decls.doc: **The bridge.** An edge is a positive one-step transition: `P⋆(1_{\{y\}})(x) > 0`.

decls.name: exists_row_pos
decls.statement: theorem exists_row_pos (S : Setting) : ∃ k, k ∈ Finset.Icc 1 S.d ∧ 0 < S.row k
decls.doc: The target row charges some index in `{1,…,d}`: it is a probability there.

decls.name: reach_dec
decls.statement: theorem reach_dec (S : Setting) (cap : Option ℕ) (j n : ℕ) : Reach S cap (.lad (j + n)) (.lad j)
decls.doc: `n` consecutive decrements: every ladder state reaches every lower one.

decls.name: reach_dec_le
decls.statement: theorem reach_dec_le (S : Setting) (cap : Option ℕ) {i j : ℕ} (h : j ≤ i) : Reach S cap (.lad i) (.lad j)

decls.name: reach_one
decls.statement: theorem reach_one (S : Setting) (cap : Option ℕ) (x : St) : Reach S cap x (.lad 1)
decls.doc: Every state reaches the ladder state `1`: down to `s₀`, wrap to `s_f`, fire the row, then decrement.

decls.name: reach_lad_none
decls.statement: theorem reach_lad_none (S : Setting) : ∀ n : ℕ, 1 ≤ n → Reach S none (.lad 1) (.lad n)
decls.doc: On the loop closure `1` reaches every ladder state, by the paper's induction: from `n` the doubling edge reaches `2n ≥ n+1`, and `2n − (n+1)` decrements land on `n+1`.

decls.name: reach_all_none
decls.statement: theorem reach_all_none (S : Setting) (x y : St) : Reach S none x y
decls.doc: **`lem:doubling_irreducible`, the graph half.** On the loop closure every state reaches every state.

decls.name: reach_pow_two
decls.statement: theorem reach_pow_two (S : Setting) : ∀ r : ℕ, 2 ^ r ≤ K → Reach S (some K) (.lad 1) (.lad (2 ^ r))
decls.doc: Doubling along the powers of two: `1 → 2 → 4 → ⋯ → 2^r`, every edge present while `2^r ≤ K`.

decls.name: reach_one_lad
decls.statement: theorem reach_one_lad (S : Setting) (hK : Even K) (hK1 : 1 ≤ K) {n : ℕ} (hn : 1 ≤ n) (hnK : n ≤ K) : Reach S (some K) (.lad 1) (.lad n)
decls.doc: **`lem:doubling_truncation_irreducible`, Step 3.** On the truncation at an even cap `K ≥ 1` the ladder state `1` reaches every ladder state `n ≤ K`.

decls.name: reach_all_some
decls.statement: theorem reach_all_some (S : Setting) (hK : Even K) (hdK : S.d ≤ K) {x y : St} (hy : OnChain (some K) y) : Reach S (some K) x y
decls.doc: **`lem:doubling_truncation_irreducible`, Steps 2–3.** On the truncation at an even cap every on-chain state reaches every on-chain state.

decls.name: PreStat
decls.statement: structure PreStat (S : Setting) (cap : Option ℕ)
decls.doc: Every field of `Stat` except positivity.

decls.name: summable_mul
decls.statement: theorem summable_mul {f : St → ℝ} (hf : ∃ C, ∀ x, |f x| ≤ C) : Summable (fun x => P.lam x * f x)

decls.name: hasSum_mul_ptFn
decls.statement: theorem hasSum_mul_ptFn (y : St) : HasSum (fun x => P.lam x * ptFn y x) (P.lam y)

decls.name: hasSum_flux
decls.statement: theorem hasSum_flux (y : St) : HasSum (fun x => P.lam x * pstar S cap (ptFn y) x) (P.lam y)
decls.doc: Total one-step flux into `y` is `λ(y)`: `inv` tested against the point mass at `y`.

decls.name: lam_pos_step
decls.statement: theorem lam_pos_step {x y : St} (h : Edge S cap x y) (hx : 0 < P.lam x) : 0 < P.lam y
decls.doc: Positivity travels along an edge.

decls.name: lam_pos_of_reach
decls.statement: theorem lam_pos_of_reach {x y : St} (h : Reach S cap x y) (hx : 0 < P.lam x) : 0 < P.lam y
decls.doc: Positivity travels along a path.

decls.name: exists_pos
decls.statement: theorem exists_pos : ∃ x, OnChain cap x ∧ 0 < P.lam x
decls.doc: A probability charges some state, and by `vanish` that state is on chain.

decls.name: pos_of_irreducible
decls.statement: theorem pos_of_irreducible (hirr : ∀ x y : St, OnChain cap y → Reach S cap x y) ⦃y : St⦄ (hy : OnChain cap y) : 0 < P.lam y
decls.doc: **`lem:doubling_irreducible`, the measure half.** An invariant probability of an irreducible chain is positive at every state of that chain.

decls.name: toStat
decls.statement: def toStat (hirr : ∀ x y : St, OnChain cap y → Reach S cap x y) : Stat S cap
decls.doc: Positivity is not an extra hypothesis: irreducibility supplies it.

decls.name: PreStat.toStatNone
decls.statement: def PreStat.toStatNone (P : PreStat S none) : Stat S none
decls.doc: On the loop closure, positivity comes free.

decls.name: PreStat.toStatSome
decls.statement: def PreStat.toStatSome {K : ℕ} (P : PreStat S (some K)) (hK : Even K) (hdK : S.d ≤ K) : Stat S (some K)
decls.doc: On the truncation at an even cap `K ≥ d`, positivity comes free.

files.title: Kac's formula on the doubling graph, from invariance alone

decls.name: hitExp_le_nat
decls.statement: theorem hitExp_le_nat (n : ℕ) (x : St) : hitExp S cap n x ≤ (n : ℝ)
decls.doc: `E(σ ∧ n) ≤ n`: the truncated hitting time is at most `n`.

decls.name: hitExp_bounded
decls.statement: theorem hitExp_bounded (n : ℕ) : ∃ C, ∀ x, |hitExp S cap n x| ≤ C

decls.name: hasSum_lam_mul_ptFn
decls.statement: theorem hasSum_lam_mul_ptFn (L : Stat S cap) (y : St) : HasSum (fun x => L.lam x * ptFn y x) (L.lam y)

decls.name: Stat.hasSum_flux_pt
decls.statement: theorem Stat.hasSum_flux_pt (L : Stat S cap) (y : St) : HasSum (fun x => L.lam x * pstar S cap (ptFn y) x) (L.lam y)
decls.doc: Total flux into `y` is `λ(y)`: invariance tested against the point mass at `y`.

decls.name: pstar_ptFn_sink
decls.statement: theorem pstar_ptFn_sink : pstar S cap (ptFn .sink) = ptFn (.lad 0)
decls.doc: **The wrap.** `P⋆ 1_{\{s_f\}} = 1_{\{s₀\}}`: the sink is entered from the source alone, with probability one.

decls.name: pstar_ptFn_src_le
decls.statement: theorem pstar_ptFn_src_le (x : St) : pstar S cap (ptFn (.lad 0)) x ≤ ptFn (.lad 1) x
decls.doc: **The decrement out of `1`.** Nothing but the state `1` flows into `s₀`.

decls.name: Stat.lam_sink_eq_src
decls.statement: theorem Stat.lam_sink_eq_src (L : Stat S cap) : L.lam .sink = L.lam (.lad 0)
decls.doc: `λ(s_f) = λ(s₀)`.

decls.name: Stat.lam_src_le_lam_one
decls.statement: theorem Stat.lam_src_le_lam_one (L : Stat S cap) : L.lam (.lad 0) ≤ L.lam (.lad 1)

decls.name: sbar
decls.statement: noncomputable def sbar (S : Setting) (cap : Option ℕ) (n : ℕ) : ℝ
decls.doc: `σ̄⁽ⁿ⁾`, the target-row average of `E(σ ∧ n)`.

decls.name: sbar_nonneg
decls.statement: theorem sbar_nonneg (n : ℕ) : 0 ≤ sbar S cap n

decls.name: sbar_mono
decls.statement: theorem sbar_mono : Monotone (sbar S cap)

decls.name: hitExp_defect
decls.statement: theorem hitExp_defect (n : ℕ) : (fun x => hitExp S cap (n + 1) x - pstar S cap (hitExp S cap n) x) = fun x => 1 - ptFn (.lad 0) x - (1 + sbar S cap n) * ptFn .sink x
decls.doc: **The defect, in closed form.** `u_{n+1} − P⋆u_n` is `1` at every ladder state, `0` at `s₀` and `−σ̄⁽ⁿ⁾` at `s_f`; as a function it is `1 − 1_{\{s₀\}} − (1+σ̄⁽ⁿ⁾) 1_{\{s_f\}}`.

decls.name: hitInt
decls.statement: noncomputable def hitInt (n : ℕ) : ℝ
decls.doc: `aₙ = ∫ E(σ ∧ n) dλ`.

decls.name: hitInt_mono
decls.statement: theorem hitInt_mono : Monotone L.hitInt

decls.name: hitInt_succ_sub
decls.statement: theorem hitInt_succ_sub (n : ℕ) : L.hitInt (n + 1) - L.hitInt n = 1 - L.lam (.lad 0) - (1 + sbar S cap n) * L.lam .sink
decls.doc: **The one-step identity.** `a_{n+1} − a_n = 1 − λ(s₀) − (1 + σ̄⁽ⁿ⁾) λ(s_f)`.

decls.name: kac_identity
decls.statement: theorem kac_identity {M B : ℝ} (hM : ∀ n : ℕ, L.hitInt n ≤ M) (hB : ∀ n : ℕ, sbar S cap n ≤ B) : L.lam (.lad 0) * (2 + ⨆ n, sbar S cap n) = 1
decls.doc: **Kac's formula on the doubling graph.** With `σ̄ := ⨆ₙ σ̄⁽ⁿ⁾`, `λ(s₀)(2 + σ̄) = 1`.

decls.name: lam_one_ge
decls.statement: theorem lam_one_ge {c : ℝ} (hc0 : 0 < c) (hc1 : c < 1) (heps : ∀ j : ℕ, 1 ≤ j → S.eps j = c / ((j : ℝ) + 1)) {M : ℝ} (hM : ∀ n : ℕ, L.hitInt n ≤ M) : (2 + S.jbar / (1 - c))⁻¹ ≤ L.lam (.lad 1)
decls.doc: **Step 6 of `cor:doubling_truncation`.** `λ_1 ≥ (2 + j̄/(1−c))^{-1}`, a bound free of `K`.

files.title: The closed-form backward length

decls.name: ladT
decls.statement: noncomputable def ladT (S : Setting) (f : ℕ → ℝ) : ℕ → ℝ | 0 => 0 | m + 1 => S.eps (m + 1) * f (2 * (m + 1)) + (1 - S.eps (m + 1)) * f m / `lem:doubling_supersolution`. -/ @[simp] theorem ladT_zero (f : ℕ → ℝ) : ladT S f 0 = 0
decls.doc: The one-step operator of the loop closure, restricted to the ladder and absorbed at `s₀`.

decls.name: ladT_succ
decls.statement: theorem ladT_succ (f : ℕ → ℝ) (m : ℕ) : ladT S f (m + 1) = S.eps (m + 1) * f (2 * (m + 1)) + (1 - S.eps (m + 1)) * f m
decls.doc: At a ladder state the operator is the two-term convex combination of `eq:doubling_policy`: the doubling edge is present at every state of the loop closure.

decls.name: ladT_mono
decls.statement: theorem ladT_mono {f g : ℕ → ℝ} (h : ∀ k, f k ≤ g k) (m : ℕ) : ladT S f m ≤ ladT S g m
decls.doc: `P⋆` is monotone, being an average over the one-step law.

decls.name: ladT_const_zero
decls.statement: theorem ladT_const_zero : ladT S (fun _ => (0 : ℝ)) = fun _ => (0 : ℝ)

decls.name: ladT_nonneg
decls.statement: theorem ladT_nonneg {f : ℕ → ℝ} (h : ∀ k, 0 ≤ f k) (m : ℕ) : 0 ≤ ladT S f m

decls.name: ladT_sub
decls.statement: theorem ladT_sub (f g : ℕ → ℝ) (m : ℕ) : ladT S (fun k => f k - g k) m = ladT S f m - ladT S g m

decls.name: ladT_lin
decls.statement: theorem ladT_lin (r t : ℝ) (f g : ℕ → ℝ) : ladT S (fun k => r * f k + t * g k) = fun m => r * ladT S f m + t * ladT S g m
decls.doc: `P⋆` is linear.

decls.name: ladT_iterate_mono
decls.statement: theorem ladT_iterate_mono {f g : ℕ → ℝ} (h : ∀ k, f k ≤ g k) (n m : ℕ) : (ladT S)^[n] f m ≤ (ladT S)^[n] g m
decls.doc: Monotonicity passes to the iterates, which is what compares the identity with a supersolution at every `n`.

decls.name: ladT_iterate_nonneg
decls.statement: theorem ladT_iterate_nonneg {f : ℕ → ℝ} (h : ∀ k, 0 ≤ f k) (n m : ℕ) : 0 ≤ (ladT S)^[n] f m

decls.name: ladT_iterate_lin
decls.statement: theorem ladT_iterate_lin (r t : ℝ) (n : ℕ) (f g : ℕ → ℝ) (m : ℕ) : (ladT S)^[n] (fun k => r * f k + t * g k) m = r * (ladT S)^[n] f m + t * (ladT S)^[n] g m
decls.doc: Linearity passes to the iterates.

decls.name: stepCost
decls.statement: def stepCost : ℕ → ℝ
decls.doc: The cost of one step: `1` at every ladder state `j ≥ 1`, `0` at the source.

decls.name: stepCost_zero
decls.statement: @[simp] theorem stepCost_zero : stepCost 0 = 0

decls.name: stepCost_succ
decls.statement: @[simp] theorem stepCost_succ (m : ℕ) : stepCost (m + 1) = 1

decls.name: stepCost_nonneg
decls.statement: theorem stepCost_nonneg (m : ℕ) : 0 ≤ stepCost m

decls.name: hitLad
decls.statement: noncomputable def hitLad (S : Setting) (n m : ℕ) : ℝ
